TITLE: Understanding the Benefits of Fine-Tuning with Real Exemplars
PROPOSAL: 
We will perform a set of experiments to understand what benefits can be gained from fine-tuning a pre-trained conditional generator with a small set of real exemplar images. We'll compare fine-tuning with and without applying a quality-based loss function that encourages the generated images to be more diverse and closely aligned with the real distribution. We will use a diverse set of regions (e.g., Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania) as our target geographic diversity. Furthermore, to assess how different levels of fine-tuning can impact the performance, we will also experiment with different number of fine-tuning iterations (3, 6, 9) and compare the model's robustness to overfitting and performance on different geographic diversity regimes.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Just fine tuning
Ablation 2 - Trade-off of Fine-tuning objective 
Batch Freeze Strategy earth-volume continuous pert fasting intentions represent guidance  
PREDICTION: 
Our hypothesis is that fine-tuning, especially combined with an objective to encourage diversity of generated data and hold constant target relation, will result in better image generation performance on a target geographic diversity regime. Moreover, we expect to find an optimal number of fine-tuning iterations that strike a balance between overfitting and performance.

COST: 2048

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incorporating Exemplar Data into Training Objective
PROPOSAL: 
We will modify the training objective of a pre-trained conditional generator to incorporate the exemplar data, in addition to the fine-tuning approach. Specifically, we will use a combination of the standard cross-entropy loss and a newly introduced exemplar loss term that encourages the generator to produce images that are close to the exemplar images. We will use a weighted sum of the two loss terms, with the weight controlling the importance of the exemplar loss. Our goal is to see if this combined approach can improve the performance of the generator on a target geographic diversity regime.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Just standard training objective
Ablation 2 - Just exemplar loss term
Batch Freeze Strategy 
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that incorporating the exemplar data into the training objective will lead to better image generation performance on a target geographic diversity regime, especially for regions that are underrepresented in the original dataset. The performance gain will depend on the weight of the exemplar loss term and the strength of the generator's representation of the exemplar images.

COST: 4096

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Exemplar Diversity on Image Generation
PROPOSAL: 
We will examine the impact of the diversity of the exemplar data on the performance of the image generator. Specifically, we will train multiple generators with different sets of exemplar images, each with a unique diversity profile (e.g., a mix of urban and rural scenes, a mix of indoor and outdoor scenes, etc.). Our goal is to see how the diversity of the exemplar data affects the performance of the generator on a target geographic diversity regime.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Just standard exemplar dataset (e.g., ImageNet)
Ablation 2 - Exemplar dataset with high urban bias
Ablation 3 - Exemplar dataset with high outdoor bias
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that the diversity of the exemplar data will have a significant impact on the performance of the generator, with the most diverse dataset leading to the best performance on the target geographic diversity regime.

COST: 8192

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Exemplar Image Size on Generator Performance
PROPOSAL: 
We will investigate the effect of the size of the exemplar images on the performance of the image generator. Specifically, we will train multiple generators with different sizes of exemplar images (e.g., 64x64, 128x128, 256x256, etc.). Our goal is to see how the size of the exemplar images affects the performance of the generator on a target geographic diversity regime.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Standard exemplar image size (e.g., 224x224)
Ablation 2 - Large exemplar image size (e.g., 512x512)
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that the size of the exemplar images will have a positive impact on the performance of the generator, with larger exemplar images leading to better performance on the target geographic diversity regime. However, we also expect that there may be diminishing returns beyond a certain size, due to increased computational complexity and potential overfitting.

COST: 16384

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Robustness of Generator to Exemplar Data Variability
PROPOSAL: 
We will assess the robustness of the image generator to variations in the exemplar data. Specifically, we will train the generator on a set of exemplar images that are perturbed in different ways (e.g., adding Gaussian noise, applying JPEG compression, etc.). Our goal is to see how the generator performs on these perturbed exemplar data and how this affects its performance on the target geographic diversity regime.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Standard exemplar data
Ablation 2 - Exemplar data with added Gaussian noise
Ablation 3 - Exemplar data with JPEG compression
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that the generator will be robust to some degree of perturbation in the exemplar data, but will struggle with more severe perturbations. We also expect that the generator will learn to adapt to the perturbations in the exemplar data and generalize better on the target geographic diversity regime.

COST: 32768

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of Learned Representations to New Geographies
PROPOSAL: 
We will evaluate the transferability of the learned representations from the image generator to new geographic regions. Specifically, we will fine-tune the generator on exemplar images from a new geographic region and evaluate its performance on that region. Our goal is to see how well the generator's learned representations generalizes to new geographic regions.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Fine-tuning on standard exemplar dataset (e.g., ImageNet)
Ablation 2 - Fine-tuning on exemplar dataset from new geographic region (e.g., Africa, Asia)
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that the generator's learned representations will transfer reasonably well to new geographic regions, especially if the new region is related to the region used to train the generator. However, we also expect some degree of performance degradation due to the lack of fine-grained details in the new region.

COST: 65536

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Combining Results and Implications for Real-World Image Generation Applications
PROPOSAL: 
We will combine the results from the previous experiments to understand the overall performance and limitations of the image generator. Our goal is to identify the key factors that influence the generator's performance and provide insights into how to improve its ability to generate high-quality images of diverse geographic regions.

CONTROLS: 
Ablation 1 - Standard training and fine-tuning protocol
Ablation 2 - Protocols explored in the previous experiments

PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that the findings from this study will provide valuable insights into the design and training of image generators for real-world applications, such as generating images for visual understanding, virtual reality, and computer vision tasks.

COST: 131072

Note: This final experiment is not a traditional experiment, but rather a meta-analysis of the results from the previous experiments. It aims to synthesize the findings and provide a deeper understanding of the image generator's performance and limitations.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Complementary Visual and Textual Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of a hybrid retriever that combines the ColPali-based visual encoder with a dense text encoder (e.g., Duet or Casanova) for the task of visual document retrieval. Train and evaluate the hybrid retriever using the LSusat-Sentence (LS-S) dataset and report retrieval performance metrics (e.g., recall, precision, and F1-score) against the standalone ColPali-based and dense text retrievers as baselines.
CONTROLS: Include ColPali-based retriever (as primary), Duet/Casanova as dense text retrievers, ablation of combining text and image encoders to identify the effect of hybridization on retrieval quality.
COST: Estimated compute: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improved retrieval quality by leveraging complementary signals from text and image encoders, but potentially lower in terms of exact retrieval metrics where image encoders excel; adjustments might fail to show monotonically better results due to complex interactions within the hybrid model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attentive Embedding Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop an attentive embedding fusion mechanism that allows the hybrid retrieval model to weigh the contributions from the ColPali-based visual encoder and the dense text encoder according to the relevance of each query-document pair. Employ a self-attention approach to aggregate the contextual representation from both encoders, ensuring efficient and adaptive fusion while preserving the interactions within the representation spaces.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Hybridizer for Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Design and experiment with an initial prototype of the "DensePattern hybridizer," which combines a lightweight dense text retriever (e.g., AnceXL, a variant of the Ance model) with a state-of-the-art vision-centric late-interaction retriever (e.g., ColPali). The hybridizer will aggregate similarity scores from both models, using principled techniques (e.g., weighting or voting schemes) and assessing model performance on various visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., VDOAK, D2R).
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: the ColPali-based retriever alone.
- Ablation 1: the AnceXL-based retriever alone.
- Baseline 2: a naive hybridization using equal weighting between models.

COST: 10,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 38 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)

PREDICTION: This initial prototype will demonstrate a strong baseline for hybridization and possibly show some improvement over the stand-alone ColPali model. Challenges in achieving sufficient gains might arise from: 
1) the performance gap between the ColPali and AnceXL models; 
2) the difficulty in designing suitable weighting schemes; 
However, potential benefits would lie in reduced latency and memory requirements for the ColPali model, given the lightweight nature of AnceXL.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Hybrid Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel, model-agnostic hybrid aggregation method that enables the combination of heterogeneous retrievers' representations without the need for tuned weighting or any modification to the base models. The proposed method, called "Iterative Cross-Modal Attention" (ICMA), involves iteratively refining attention weights between two modalities to pool the final aggregated representation. ICMA will be evaluated in conjunction with the DensePattern hybridizer on the same benchmarks.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: the DensePattern hybridizer using equal weighting (from Proposal 1).
- Ablation 1: the DensePattern hybridizer using no weighting or voting schemes.
- Baseline 2: the ColPali-based retriever alone.

COST: 5,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 19 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)

PREDICTION: Employing the ICMA aggregation method could enable the DensePattern hybridizer to aggregate the complementary signals between the multiple representation spaces, overcoming the deficiencies of simple weighted or voting schemes. Its model-agnostic nature would make it applicable to both single-vector and multi-vector models. This might result in further performance improvements, potentially helping mitigate the limitations of purely vision-centric approaches.

ACTION: REVISE
 TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Hybridizer for Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Revise the Lightweight Dense Text Hybridizer to utilize the Iterative Cross-Modal Attention (ICMA) aggregation method (Proposal 2) when combining the similarity scores from both the lightweight dense text retriever (e.g., AnceXL) and the ColPali-based retriever. Assess the effects of leveraging ICMA on the hybridizer's performance.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: the ColPali-based retriever alone.
- Ablation 1: the AnceXL-based retriever alone.
- Baseline 2: the original densePattern hybridizer using equal weighting (from Proposal 1).

COST: 3,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 11 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)

PREDICTION: Upgrading the densePattern hybridizer with ICMA is expected to improve its overall performance, possibly closing the gap with more complex, but less scalable, models. Improved cross-modal attention weights might facilitate better representation pooling, ultimately benefiting the retrieval outcomes.

PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate novel evaluation protocols and metrics for comparing the strengths and weaknesses of heterogeneous multi-vector representations. Metrics will be developed to assess the performance of the hybridizer under various dimensionalities, scales, and distribution characteristics of the representation spaces after hybridization. Evaluate the hybridizer with these customized metrics to provide a more nuanced understanding of its effectiveness in different scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Index Pruning and Quantization Optimization
PROPOSAL: Investigate methods to optimize the memory and computational requirements of the hybrid retriever, particularly for large-scale applications. This will involve exploring index pruning techniques (e.g., removing redundant or irrelevant data) and quantization methods (e.g., reducing precision of dense vector representations) to improve the hybridizer's efficiency while maintaining its accuracy. Evaluate the effects of these optimization techniques on the retriever's performance and storage requirements.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: the hybridizer without pruning or quantization.
- Baseline 2: the hybridizer with random pruning and quantization.
COST: 8,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 30 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)

PREDICTION: Index pruning and quantization could significantly reduce the computational requirements of the hybrid retriever, making it more suitable for production environments with limited resources. However, these optimizations may introduce new challenges, such as decreased accuracy due to information loss or reduced effectiveness of the iterative attention mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Late-Interaction vs. Early-Interaction Architectures for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of employing either late-interaction (e.g., ColPali) or early-interaction (e.g., MALP) architectures for the lightweight dense text component in the hybridizer. This comparison will involve modifying the AnceXL-based retriever to use either late- or early-interaction attention mechanisms and evaluating the performance differences in the hybrid setting.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: AnceXL with late-interaction attention (as originally used).
- Baseline 2: AnceXL with early-interaction attention (new variant for this experiment).
COST: 6,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 23 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)

PREDICTION: This comparison may provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different interaction architectures for hybrid multimodal retrieval and help guiding future research on optimal architectures for such systems.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Conduct an investigation on how to strike an optimal balance between the emphasis on text and image modalities for the hybrid retriever. Propose and evaluate different methods to align and normalize the representation spaces of the two modalities, aiming to improve the overall quality of the hybrid retrieval results. These methods may include modality-specific normalization, cross-modal proximity Crushers, and attention-based alignment.

Improved cross-modal attention weights might facilitate better representation pooling, ultimately benefiting the retrieval outcomes.

PROPOSAL 2: Model-Agnostic Hybrid Aggregation
Introduce a novel, model-agnostic hybrid aggregation method that enables the combination of heterogeneous retrievers' representations without the need for tuned weighting or any modification to the base models. The proposed method, called "Iterative Cross-Modal Attention" (ICMA), involves iteratively refining attention weights between two modalities to pool the final aggregated representation. ICMA will be evaluated in conjunction with the DensePattern hybridizer on the same benchmarks.
Controls: - Baseline 1: the DensePattern hybridizer using equal weighting (from Proposal 1).
- Ablation 1: the DensePattern hybridizer using no weighting or voting schemes.
- Baseline 2: the ColPali-based retriever alone.
Estimated cost: 5,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 19 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)
Prediction: Employing the ICMA aggregation method could enable the DensePattern hybridizer to aggregate the complementary signals between the multiple representation spaces, overcoming the deficiencies of simple weighted or voting schemes. Its model-agnostic nature would make it applicable to both single-vector and multi-vector models. This might result in further performance improvements, potentially helping mitigate the limitations of purely vision-centric approaches.

PROPOSAL 3: Heterogeneous Multi-Vector Evaluation
Design and evaluate novel evaluation protocols and metrics for comparing the strengths and weaknesses of heterogeneous multi-vector representations. Metrics will be developed to assess the performance of the hybridizer under various dimensionalities, scales, and distribution characteristics of the representation spaces after hybridization. Evaluate the hybridizer with these customized metrics to provide a more nuanced understanding of its effectiveness in different scenarios.
Controls: - Baseline 1: standard retrieval metrics (e.g., Recall, Precision, F1-score).
- Baseline 2: retrieval metrics tuned for high-dimensional and scaled representations (e.g., Average Precision among top-N documents).
Estimated cost: 4,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 15 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)
Prediction: A deeper understanding of the hybridizer's performance under various representation conditions should help in interpreting the results and providing insight on best practices for handling heterogeneous representations in the future; accurate representation to the observation after after calculating; more sensitivity complicated descriptions of docs availability

PROPOSAL 4: Index Pruning and Quantization Optimization
Investigate methods to optimize the memory and computational requirements of the hybrid retriever, particularly for large-scale applications. This will involve exploring index pruning techniques (e.g., removing redundant or irrelevant data) and quantization methods (e.g., reducing precision of dense vector representations) to improve the hybridizer's efficiency while maintaining its accuracy. Evaluate the effects of these optimization techniques on the retriever's performance and storage requirements.
Controls: - Baseline 1: the hybridizer without pruning or quantization.
- Baseline 2: the hybridizer with random pruning and quantization.
Estimated cost: 8,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 30 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)
Prediction: Index pruning and quantization could significantly reduce the computational requirements of the hybrid retriever, making it more suitable for production environments with limited resources. However, these optimizations may introduce new challenges, such as decreased accuracy due to information loss or reduced effectiveness of the iterative attention mechanism.

PROPOSAL 5: Exploring Late-Interaction vs. Early-Interaction Architectures for Hybrid Retrieval
Investigate the impact of employing either late-interaction (e.g., ColPali) or early-interaction (e.g., MALP) architectures for the lightweight dense text component in the hybridizer. This comparison will involve modifying the AnceXL-based retriever to use either late- or early-interaction attention mechanisms and evaluating the performance differences in the hybrid setting.
Controls: - Baseline 1: AnceXL with late-interaction attention (as originally used).
- Baseline 2: AnceXL with early-interaction attention (new variant for this experiment).
Estimated cost: 6,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 23 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)
Prediction: This comparison may provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different interaction architectures for hybrid multimodal retrieval and help guiding future research on optimal architectures for such systems.

PROPOSAL 6: Study on Modal Balance and Alignment for Hybrid Retrieval
Integrate all the findings and proposed improvements from the previous experiments into this proposal, incorporating the Model-Agnostic Hybrid Aggregation, heterogeneous multi-vector evaluation, index pruning and quantization optimization, late-interaction vs. early-interaction architectures. Then use the Study on Modal Balance and Alignment to find the right architecture parameter setting.
Controls: - Baseline 1: the hybridizer without modal balance or alignment techniques.
- Baseline 2: standard V`Cosine embedding-based alignment strategy.
Estimated cost: 10,000 GPU-hours ( approx. 38 days with 200 NVIDIA V100 GPUs)
Prediction: By incorporating the various improvement strategies, the hybridizer can be significantly enhanced, and the study on modal balance and alignment can help optimize the model's performance and robustness, potentially leading to state-of-the-art results on visual document retrieval tasks.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Baseline Evaluation of State-of-the-art Visual Document Retrieval Models
PROPOSAL: Implement and evaluate the performance of ColPali-based and ColBERT-based multimodal encoders on public visual document retrieval benchmarks, such as Doc2Query and LEADSDataset, and compare their results with existing state-of-the-art models. We will also examine their computational efficiency, storage requirements, and online latency for scalable deployment.
CONTROLS: ColBERT with semantic text encoder, BM25 with sparse lexical representation, and dense text retrievers like DPR.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: ColPali-based and ColBERT-based models should achieve state-of-the-art results, but ColPali may have higher latency and storage requirements due to the massive length and dimensionality of its query and document representations.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Retrieval as a Complementary Channel for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a lightweight dense text retriever, such as the MiniLM model from the Berkeley Embeddings Wiki, that can be used in conjunction with the ColPali-based or ColBERT-based multimodal encoders to enhance the retrieval performance. We will fine-tune the MiniLM model on a sub-set of the training data used for the visual document retrieval models, and evaluate its performance on the same benchmarks.
CONTROLS: The standalone MiniLM model, and the ColPali-based or ColBERT-based multimodal encoder as the primary retriever.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The lightweight dense text retriever should provide a complementary signal that improves the overall retrieval performance, especially in cases where the visual signal is ambiguous or noisy. However, its impact may be limited if the gap between the dense and visual representations is too large.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Retrieval as a Complementary Channel for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a lightweight dense text retriever, such as the MiniLM model from the Berkeley Embeddings Wiki, that can be used in conjunction with the ColPali-based or ColBERT-based multimodal encoders to enhance the retrieval performance. We will fine-tune the MiniLM model on a sub-set of the training data used for the visual document retrieval models, and evaluate its performance on the same benchmarks. Additionally, we will investigate the impact of different aggregation strategies, such as concatenation, element-wise sum, and weighted sum, to combine the outputs of the visual and textual retrievers.
CONTROLS: The standalone MiniLM model, the ColPali-based or ColBERT-based multimodal encoder as the primary retriever, and different aggregation strategies.
COST: 70 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The lightweight dense text retriever should provide a complementary signal that improves the overall retrieval performance, and the aggregation strategies will help to identify the most effective way to combine the outputs of the visual and textual retrievers.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Attention-based Aggregation for Combining Visual and Textual Retrieval Outputs
PROPOSAL: Implement attention-based aggregation mechanisms, such as attention on top of the outputs of the two retrievers or using attention to select relevant components from the outputs, to combine the textual and visual retriever outputs in a more robust and interpretable manner. We will evaluate the performance of the aggregated retrievers on the same benchmarks and compare them with the results from the concatenation and other aggregation strategies.
CONTROLS: Different attention mechanisms, such as self-attention and dot-product attention, and the aggregation strategies from proposal 2.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The attention-based aggregation mechanisms will help to learn more effective and task-specific weights for combining the outputs of the visual and textual retrievers, leading to further improvements in the retrieval performance.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigation of Latency and Storage Overheads for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Systematically analyze and compare the latency and storage overheads of the ColPali-based and ColBERT-based multimodal encoders, the dense text retriever, and their combinations, using real-world data and deployment scenarios. We will measure the computation time, memory usage, and indexing time for each retriever, and evaluate the trade-offs between retrieval performance, latency, and storage requirements.
CONTROLS: The standalone ColPali-based and ColBERT-based multimodal encoders, the dense text retriever, and different aggregation strategies.
COST: 90 GPU-hours (excluding real-world deployment and measurement)
PREDICTION: The analysis will reveal the actual latency and storage overheads of the different retrievers, enabling informed decisions on when to use hybrid retrieval, when to use a single text or vision-based retriever, and how to balance performance and efficiency in real-world deployment scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Robustness and Sensitivity Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Perform a robustness and sensitivity analysis of the hybrid retrieval approach by evaluating its performance under different conditions, such as perturbations in the input data (e.g., adversarial examples or noisy input), varying levels of overlap between the textual and visual retriever outputs, and out-of-distribution queries. We will use metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and calibration error to assess the robustness of the hybrid retrieval system.
CONTROLS: Different perturbation levels, varying levels of overlap, and different out-of-distribution queries.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The analysis will reveal the robustness and sensitivity of the hybrid retrieval approach, identifying areas where it may be vulnerable to contamination or failure, and enabling the development of more robust and reliable systems.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Robustness and Sensitivity Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Perform a more comprehensive robustness and sensitivity analysis of the hybrid retrieval approach by evaluating its performance under different conditions, such as perturbations in the input data (e.g., adversarial examples or noisy input), varying levels of overlap between the textual and visual retriever outputs, and out-of-distribution queries. Additionally, we will investigate the impact of different aggregation strategies, such as those proposed in proposal 3, on the robustness and performance of the hybrid retrieval system. We will use metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and calibration error to assess the robustness of the hybrid retrieval system.
CONTROLS: Different perturbation levels, varying levels of overlap, different out-of-distribution queries, and different aggregation strategies.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised analysis will provide a more thorough understanding of the robustness and sensitivity of the hybrid retrieval approach, and help to identify the most effective strategies for building robust and reliable systems.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Hybrid Visual Document Retrieval and Summarization
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of training a single model that can perform both hybrid visual document retrieval and document summarization tasks. We will use multitask learning to train a model that can learn to retrieve relevant documents and generate summaries for them, leveraging the shared structure between the two tasks.
CONTROLS: The baseline models for document retrieval and summarization, and different multitask learning strategies.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Multitask learning could potentially improve the performance of hybrid visual document retrieval by learning to prioritize salient information for both retrieval and summarization, but may also introduce training difficulties due to the added complexity of the summarization task.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of pre-trained models for visual document retrieval, such as those pre-trained on image recognition or object detection tasks, and evaluate their effectiveness in transferring to visual document retrieval tasks. We will explore fine-tuning these pre-trained models on smaller amounts of labeled data, and evaluate their performance on the same benchmarks as the baseline models.
CONTROLS: Different pre-trained models and fine-tuning strategies, as well as the baseline models.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Transfer learning could potentially improve the performance of visual document retrieval by leveraging pre-trained models, but may also introduce overfitting or domain mismatch issues if not properly fine-tuned.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Baseline Evaluation of State-of-the-art Visual Document Retrieval Models
PROPOSAL: Revise and expand the baseline evaluation to include a more comprehensive comparison of the performance of ColPali-based and ColBERT-based multimodal encoders, the lightweight dense text retriever, and their combinations, under different conditions such as different aggregation strategies, transfer learning, and multitask learning. We will also investigate the impact of these factors on the performance of the hybrid retrieval system and provide a more detailed analysis of the results.
CONTROLS: The revised set of baseline models, including ColPali-based and ColBERT-based multimodal encoders, the lightweight dense text retriever, and their combinations, as well as different aggregation strategies, transfer learning, and multitask learning.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised baseline evaluation will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of the different models and retrieval strategies, and will help to identify the most effective approaches for visual document retrieval.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Angles-First Search for Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: Implement an "angles-first" search algorithm that restricts the direction of action optimization to lie within the sparsest orthogonal directions in the action space, identified using the PCA-Sparse transformation. This approach aims to efficiently navigate the high-dimensional Q-function landscape and escape local optima by focusing exploration in the most informative directions.
CONTROLS: Baseline implementation of gradient ascent on the Q-function, with and without PCA-Sparse direction optimization
COST: 100 GPU-hours (approximating PCA-Sparse, and running gradient ascent with/without the optimization)
PREDICTION: Improved sample efficiency over plain gradient ascent, with precise escape from local optima in simulation; however, it may struggle with very high-dimensional action spaces where PCA-Sparse converges slowly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Geodesic Exploration for Scalable Q-Function Optimization
PROPOSAL: Develop a geodesic exploration method that exploits the Riemannian geometry of the action space to efficiently optimize the Q-function by exploring the space along geodesic paths, which are the shortest paths on the manifold of the action space, using the Levi-Civita connection. We will use the Matrix Logarithm to compute the geodesic distance and paths.
CONTROLS: Compare with the angles-first search from proposal 1, and a baseline gradient-based optimization on a fixed Euclidean metric
COST: 150 GPU-hours (approximating geodesics, and computing exponential maps)
PREDICTION: This method will allow for a significant reduction in the number of evaluations required to find optimal actions, especially in high-dimensional action spaces, due to the efficiency of geodesic exploration, but it may be computationally expensive for large numbers of actions due to the cost of matrix logarithm computation.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Geodesic Exploration for Scalable Q-Function Optimization (Iteration: Approximating Matrix Logarithms with BFGS)
PROPOSAL: Replace the computationally expensive matrix logarithm approximation with a preconditioned BFGS method to iteratively build a quadratic approximation of the Hessian of the Q-function, allowing for approximate geodesics without explicitly computing the matrix logarithm.
CONTROLS: Compare with the previous version of the geodesic method (with matrix Logarithm), and retain the baseline gradient-based optimization on a fixed Euclidean metric
COST: 120 GPU-hours (comparatively less expensive than approximating matrix logarithm, and with  fewer function evaluations)
PREDICTION: This revised geodesic exploration method will provide a substantial reduction in computational cost without sacrificing much in terms of efficiency, but will likely require some additional tuning of hyperparameters for optimal performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Efficient Angles-First Search for Continuous Action Spaces (Improved Directionality)

CONTROLS: Compare with the original PCA-Sparse angles-first search and the revised geodesic exploration method
COST: 50 GPU-hours (PCA-Sparse, sparse projection, and same baseline optimizations)
PREDICTION: This refined angles-first search will achieve improved convergence rates and escape local optima more efficiently than the original method, especially when the Q-function has complex structures.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Trajectorial Preference Functions for Actor-Free Optimization
PROPOSAL: We will analyze the performance of value-based methods that use new, actor-free optimization techniques, specifically drawing inspiration from the Trajectorial Preference Functions (TPFs) that were initially introduced as an improvement upon Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG). We will attempt to replicate and improve upon this model by tackling continuous action spaces of various dimensions through modifying methods such as stochastic trajectory optimization. This could allow us to alleviate the computations associated with discretization while maintaining a high degree of accuracy.
CONTROLS: A baseline Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) method, a simpler DQN method (which we consider not to perform well under similar conditions), and possibly monte carlo tree search with improved node initialization
COST: 20,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our initial tests suggest that the algorithm might be quite competitive with established actor-critic methods for discrete action spaces; we predict a higher success rate than DQN in the lower complexity tasks under scrutiny, an almost parity with DDPG in these same complexity layers.

However, our algorithm might perform poorly (or be more chaotic) when we're comparing against DDPG on larger and more complex tasks, which run into non-convex action spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improved Approximation of the Maximizing Action through Distributional Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: We will develop a distributional off-policy actor-free algorithm for the game theoretically founded Q-function, aiming to find a better approximation of the value function. This algorithm incorporates distributional Q-Learning (DQfD), where we'll have actions taken from the Q's learned distribution, which allows a direct lookahead search for comparatively precise bounds on policy returns, refocusing the benefits seen in work such as Soft Actor-Critic (SAC).
CONTROLS: Investigating the efficacy of traditional Q-function approximations, including standard deterministic DQN and SAC
COST: 15,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our distributional version of the actor-free algorithm could possibly compute the optimal action value better than our Trajectorial Preference Functions (TPFs) under scenarios where available actions amount to considerable (multiplicative, rather than additive, risk). More concretely, DQfD may demonstrate competitive action-value computing capabilities when both actions are away from very low (non-tractable multi-modalities) probability densities.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Improved Approximation of the Maximizing Action through Distributional Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: We will modify the previous proposal by incorporating a novel sampling strategy to further improve the accuracy of the distributional Q-Learning. Specifically, we will use theッシュ[Squeeze]-sampling trick, which involves approximating the Q-value distribution through a combination of a mixture of modes and an UTM-convex regularizer. This should allow us to better capture the nuances of the Q-function in high-dimensional action spaces.
CONTROLS: Investigating the efficacy of different sampling strategies, including THC sampling and normalizing flow zsampling
COST: 18,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating this new sampling strategy, we predict that our algorithm will outperform previous actor-free methods, especially in high-dimensional action spaces where traditional Q-function approximations tend to falter. However, we also expect that the added complexity may lead to increased computational requirements, potentially offsetting some of these gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Robustness of Actor-Free Methods to Mode Collapse and Non-Convexity
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of the two actor-free methods proposed so far to mode collapse and non-convexity, two common issues that arise in high-dimensional action spaces. We will use a range of experiments with synthetic datasets of increasing dimensionality and complexity, and analyze the agents' ability to discover and adapt to different modes and policies.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the robustness of traditional Q-function approximations, including DQN and SAC
COST: 12,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our analysis may reveal that both methods are prone to mode collapse in high-dimensional action spaces, but that the distributional Q-Learning method is more robust to this issue. Additionally, we expect that the Trajectorial Preference Functions method will tend to get stuck in local optima due to its non-convex nature.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Applying Actor-Free Methods to Constrained Continuous Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: We will adapt the two actor-free methods proposed so far to constrained continuous control tasks, where the action space is limited by safety constraints. We will use a range of synthetic and simulated datasets that involve constrained control, and evaluate the agents' ability to adapt to these constraints while still optimizing their performance.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and TD3, on the same tasks
COST: 25,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our adaptation of the actor-free methods may allow them to outperform standard actor-critic methods in constrained control tasks, by leveraging the structure of the constraints to improve their exploration and exploitation trade-off. However, we also predict that the Trajectorial Preference Functions method may struggle with the non-convex nature of the task, while the distributional Q-Learning method may benefit from its ability to handle complex value functions.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Improving Actor-Free Methods with Hierarchical Exploration-Exploitation
PROPOSAL: We will modify the distributional Q-Learning method to incorporate hierarchical exploration-exploitation, by using a meta-policy to select a sub-policy that can adapt to different parts of the value function. This should allow us to better balance exploration and exploitation, and improve the agency's ability to adapt to high-dimensional action spaces.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the efficacy of standard hierarchy-free exploration-exploitation methods, such as epsilon-greedy and Thompson sampling
COST: 20,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our modified distributional Q-Learning method may allow it to outperform the standard method on a range of synthetic and simulated tasks, by leveraging the structure of the value function to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off. However, we also expect that the added complexity of the meta-policy may lead to increased computational requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Guarantees for Actor-Free Methods
PROPOSAL: We will provide theoretical guarantees for the convergence and optimality of the actor-free methods proposed so far. Specifically, we will derive bounds on the regret, value function convergence rates, and optimality gaps of the two actor-free methods. These results will help to establish the theoretical foundations of actor-free methods and provide insights into their design and analysis.
CONTROLS: Developing theoretical guarantees for standard actor-critic methods, such as DDPG and SAC
COST: 8,000 GPU-hours (note: this proposal does not require significant computational resources)
PREDICTION: Our theoretical guarantees may confirm that the actor-free methods are able to achieve comparable or better performance than standard actor-critic methods, while also providing insights into the conditions under which they are most effective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Actor-Free Methods with Actor-Critic Methods on Real-World Tasks
PROPOSAL: We will compare the performance of the actor-free methods proposed so far with standard actor-critic methods on real-world tasks, including robotic manipulation and perception, autonomous driving, and recommender systems. We will evaluate the performance of the agents on these tasks using metrics such as task completion rate, success rate, and reward.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and SAC, on the same real-world tasks
COST: 35,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our comparison may reveal that the actor-free methods are able to achieve comparable or better performance than standard actor-critic methods on certain real-world tasks, while also providing insights into the conditions under which they are most effective. However, we also expect that the complexity and domain-specific requirements of real-world tasks may create challenges for the actor-free methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Exploration in Actor-Free Methods
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the role of exploration in actor-free methods by comparing the performance of different exploration strategies, such as epsilon-greedy, entropy regulation, and Gaussian noise injection. We will evaluate the performance of the agents on synthetic and real-world tasks using metrics such as task completion rate, success rate, and reward.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and SAC, with different exploration strategies
COST: 30,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our investigation may reveal that the choice of exploration strategy has a significant impact on the performance of actor-free methods, and that some exploration strategies are more effective than others in certain tasks and domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Actor-Free Methods
PROPOSAL: We will develop a unified framework that encompasses the various actor-free methods proposed so far, and provides a general approach for designing and analyzing actor-free algorithms. The framework will provide a common language and set of tools for understanding the strengths and limitations of actor-free methods, and will facilitate the development of new actor-free methods that can be applied to a wide range of tasks and domains.
CONTROLS: Evaluating the performance of the unified framework on a variety of tasks and domains
COST: 40,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our unified framework may provide a new and powerful tool for designing and analyzing actor-free methods, and may enable the development of more effective and efficient actor-free algorithms for a wide range of tasks and domains.

PROPOSAL 1: Investigating the Efficacy of Trajectorial Preference Functions for Actor-Free Optimization
We will analyze the performance of value-based methods that use new, actor-free optimization techniques, specifically drawing inspiration from the Trajectorial Preference Functions (TPFs) that were initially introduced as an improvement upon Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG). We will attempt to replicate and improve upon this model by tackling continuous action spaces of various dimensions through modifying methods such as stochastic trajectory optimization. This could allow us to alleviate the computations associated with discretization while maintaining a high degree of accuracy.
Controls: A baseline Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) method, a simpler DQN method (which we consider not to perform well under similar conditions), and possibly monte carlo tree search with improved node initialization
Estimated cost: 20,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our initial tests suggest that the algorithm might be quite competitive with established actor-critic methods for discrete action spaces; we predict a higher success rate than DQN in the lower complexity tasks under scrutiny, an almost parity with DDPG in these same complexity layers.

However, our algorithm might perform poorly (or be more chaotic) when we're comparing against DDPG on larger and more complex tasks, which run into non-convex action spaces.

PROPOSAL 2: Improved Approximation of the Maximizing Action through Distributional Q-Learning
We will develop a distributional off-policy actor-free algorithm for the game theoretically founded Q-function, aiming to find a better approximation of the value function. This algorithm incorporates distributional Q-Learning (DQfD), where we'll have actions taken from the Q's learned distribution, which allows a direct lookahead search for comparatively precise bounds on policy returns, refocusing the benefits seen in work such as Soft Actor-Critic (SAC).
Controls: Investigating the efficacy of traditional Q-function approximations, including standard deterministic DQN and SAC
Estimated cost: 15,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our distributional version of the actor-free algorithm could possibly compute the optimal action value better than our Trajectorial Preference Functions (TPFs) under scenarios where available actions amount to considerable (multiplicative, rather than additive, risk). More concretely, DQfD may demonstrate competitive action-value computing capabilities when both actions are away from very low (non-tractable multi-modalities) probability densities.

PROPOSAL 3: Analyzing the Robustness of Actor-Free Methods to Mode Collapse and Non-Convexity
We will evaluate the robustness of the two actor-free methods proposed so far to mode collapse and non-convexity, two common issues that arise in high-dimensional action spaces. We will use a range of experiments with synthetic datasets of increasing dimensionality and complexity, and analyze the agents' ability to discover and adapt to different modes and policies.
Controls: Evaluating the robustness of traditional Q-function approximations, including DQN and SAC
Estimated cost: 12,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our analysis may reveal that both methods are prone to mode collapse in high-dimensional action spaces, but that the distributional Q-Learning method is more robust to this issue. Additionally, we expect that the Trajectorial Preference Functions method will tend to get stuck in local optima due to its non-convex nature.

PROPOSAL 4: Applying Actor-Free Methods to Constrained Continuous Control Tasks
We will adapt the two actor-free methods proposed so far to constrained continuous control tasks, where the action space is limited by safety constraints. We will use a range of synthetic and simulated datasets that involve constrained control, and evaluate the agents' ability to adapt to these constraints while still optimizing their performance.
Controls: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and TD3, on the same tasks
Estimated cost: 25,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our adaptation of the actor-free methods may allow them to outperform standard actor-critic methods in constrained control tasks, by leveraging the structure of the constraints to improve their exploration and exploitation trade-off. However, we also predict that the Trajectorial Preference Functions method may struggle with the non-convex nature of the task, while the distributional Q-Learning method may benefit from its ability to handle complex value functions.

PROPOSAL 5: Theoretical Guarantees for Actor-Free Methods
We will provide theoretical guarantees for the convergence and optimality of the actor-free methods proposed so far. Specifically, we will derive bounds on the regret, value function convergence rates, and optimality gaps of the two actor-free methods. These results will help to establish the theoretical foundations of actor-free methods and provide insights into their design and analysis.
Controls: Developing theoretical guarantees for standard actor-critic methods, such as DDPG and SAC
Estimated cost: 8,000 GPU-hours (note: this proposal does not require significant computational resources)
Prediction: Our theoretical guarantees may confirm that the actor-free methods are able to achieve comparable or better performance than standard actor-critic methods, while also providing insights into the conditions under which they are most effective.

PROPOSAL 6: Comparing Actor-Free Methods with Actor-Critic Methods on Real-World Tasks
We will compare the performance of the actor-free methods proposed so far with standard actor-critic methods on real-world tasks, including robotic manipulation and perception, autonomous driving, and recommender systems. We will evaluate the performance of the agents on these tasks using metrics such as task completion rate, success rate, and reward.
Controls: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and SAC, on the same real-world tasks
Estimated cost: 35,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our comparison may reveal that the actor-free methods are able to achieve comparable or better performance than standard actor-critic methods on certain real-world tasks, while also providing insights into the conditions under which they are most effective. However, we also expect that the complexity and domain-specific requirements of real-world tasks may create challenges for the actor-free methods.

PROPOSAL 7: Investigating the Role of Exploration in Actor-Free Methods
We will investigate the role of exploration in actor-free methods by comparing the performance of different exploration strategies, such as epsilon-greedy, entropy regulation, and Gaussian noise injection. We will evaluate the performance of the agents on synthetic and real-world tasks using metrics such as task completion rate, success rate, and reward.
Controls: Evaluating the performance of standard actor-critic methods, including DDPG and SAC, with different exploration strategies
Estimated cost: 30,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our investigation may reveal that the choice of exploration strategy has a significant impact on the performance of actor-free methods, and that some exploration strategies are more effective than others in certain tasks and domains.

PROPOSAL 8: A Unified Framework for Actor-Free Methods
We will develop a unified framework that encompasses the various actor-free methods proposed so far, and provides a general approach for designing and analyzing actor-free algorithms. The framework will provide a common language and set of tools for understanding the strengths and limitations of actor-free methods, and will facilitate the development of new actor-free methods that can be applied to a wide range of tasks and domains.
Controls: Evaluating the performance of the unified framework on a variety of tasks and domains
Estimated cost: 40,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Our unified framework may provide a new and powerful tool for designing and analyzing actor-free methods, and may enable the development of more effective and efficient actor-free algorithms for a wide range of tasks and domains.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient, Actor-Free Value Function Maximization via Parallelized, Adaptive Sampling
PROPOSAL: Employ a novel adaptive sampling strategy that leverages multiple level sets to efficiently find the maximizing action in the value function. The sampling will be performed in parallel using multiple GPUs to accelerate computation. The approach will utilize a learned model to predict the value function's gradient, guiding the sampling towards promising regions.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing actor-free methods such as Dreamer-V and naïve grid search.
COST: Estimated 10,000 GPU-hours on 8 V100 GPUs.
PREDICTION: It is predicted that the new adaptive sampling strategy will significantly outperform existing actor-free methods in terms of convergence speed while maintaining reasonable compute efficiency, but may struggle on highly non-convex value functions with many local maxima.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Improved, parallelized Adaptive Sampling with Early Stopping and Quality Control
PROPOSAL: Revise the adaptive sampling strategy to incorporate early stopping and quality control mechanisms. The strategy will now stop sampling when it reaches a predefined threshold or when the gradient of the value function becomes negligible, reducing unnecessary computations. To ensure the quality of the sampled maxima, we will implement additional checks to verify whether the sampled actions indeed maximize the value function.
CONTROLS: Compare this revised strategy with the original adaptive sampling method and existing actor-free methods.
COST: Estimated 2,000 GPU-hours on 8 V100 GPUs (as a revision of the original proposal).
PREDICTION: The revised adaptive sampling strategy is expected to lead to more efficient computation and sample higher-quality maxima, but may potentially miss the global maximum in very flat regions of the value function.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Updating Proposal 1: Improved, Parallelized Adaptive Sampling with Early Stopping and Quality Control
PROPOSAL: Revise the adaptive sampling strategy to incorporate early stopping and quality control mechanisms. The strategy will now stop sampling when it reaches a predefined threshold or when the gradient of the value function becomes negligible, reducing unnecessary computations. To ensure the quality of the sampled maxima, we will implement additional checks to verify whether the sampled actions indeed maximize the value function.
CONTROLS: Compare this revised strategy with the original adaptive sampling method and existing actor-free methods.
COST: Estimated 2,000 GPU-hours on 8 V100 GPUs (as a revision of the original proposal).
PREDICTION: The revised adaptive sampling strategy is expected to lead to more efficient computation and sample higher-quality maxima, but may potentially miss the global maximum in very flat regions of the value function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unbiased Stochastic Gradient Estimation for Value Function Maximization
PROPOSAL: Introduce an unbiased stochastic gradient estimation approach to leverage a small batch of parameter space explorations through noisy but unbiased estimators of the stochastic gradient of the value function.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing stochastic gradient methods and the revised adaptive sampling strategy.
COST: Estimated 8,000 GPU-hours on 8 V100 GPUs.
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to provide faster convergence in the early stages and enable more aggressive stochastic optimization in the exploration-exploitation trade-off.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Stochastic Optimization via Importance Sampling and Sequential Monte Carlo
PROPOSAL: Use importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo methods to drive the stochastic optimization process, efficiently exploring areas of the parameter space that are most relevant to maximizing the value function. This combines the benefits of unbiased gradient estimation with more efficient exploration of the search space.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing stochastic gradient methods and the revised adaptive sampling strategy from proposal 1.
COST: Estimated 15,000 GPU-hours on 16 V100 GPUs.
PREDICTION: This approach should enable faster convergence and improve the overall efficiency of stochastic optimization, but may require adjustments to balancing exploration-exploitation trade-offs.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Updating Proposal 2: Efficient Stochastic Optimization via Importance Sampling and Sequential Monte Carlo with Regularization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a regularization term to the importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo optimization process to prevent overfitting and ensure the sampling process remains balanced across the search space. This update could be as simple as adding a L2 regularization term to the objective function or more complex methods such as dropout in the sampling process.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal 2 and with proposal 1 to investigate changes in optimization performance.
COST: Estimated additional 3,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 2.
PREDICTION: Regularization is expected to improve the reliability of the optimization process and prevent overfitting, but may also lead to a slight reduction in expected performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Q-Function Modification to Simplify Gradient-based Optimization
PROPOSAL: Modify the Q-function to make gradient-based optimization more efficient by transforming the Q-function into a more easily computable and differentiable form. This modification would simplify the optimization process by reducing the dimensionality of the problem and making it more amenable to gradient methods.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal 1 and proposal 2, focusing on changes in computation efficiency.
COST: Estimated 10,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 1.
PREDICTION: This modification is expected to simplify the optimization process, potentially allowing for more efficient convergence and wider applicability of gradient-based methods. However, the performance may suffer due to the introduced simplifications.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Updating Proposal 3: The Q-Function Modification with a Focus on Preserving Accuracy
PROPOSAL: Refine the Q-function modification to preserve the original Q-function's accuracy while enabling efficient gradient-based optimization. This can be achieved by introducing a learnable mapping between the original Q-function and its more computationally friendly version. The goal is to ensure that the simplified Q-function continues to accurately capture the underlying relationships in the original Q-function.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised proposal 3 with the original proposal 1 and proposal 2, focusing on changes in both efficiency and accuracy.
COST: Estimated additional 5,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 3.
PREDICTION: The revised Q-function modification is expected to strike a better balance between optimization efficiency and accuracy preservation, but may require careful tuning of the learnable mapping.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Actor-Free Value Function Maximization via Active Exploration and Q-Value Clustering
PROPOSAL: Implement an active exploration strategy to select strategic perturbations of the input that maximize the expected value of the Q-function. Additionally, cluster Q-values to identify regions of high confidence and focus optimization efforts on areas with lower confidence. This would enable the algorithm to adapt to changing value functions and cope with uncertainty in the Q-value estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing actor-free methods and the revised proposal 3, focusing on exploration-exploitation trade-offs.
COST: Estimated 20,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 1.
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to improve the robustness of actor-free value function maximization by adaptively adjusting the exploration strategy and leveraging Q-value clustering to target areas with high uncertainty. However, it may come at the cost of increased computational requirements due to the active exploration component.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Model-Based Actor-Free Optimization
PROPOSAL: Use a learned probabilistic model of the value function to efficiently approximate the Q-value function and guide optimization. The learned model would provide a compact, but accurate representation of the value function, enabling fast exploration and exploitation.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing actor-free methods and the revised proposal 3, focusing on optimization speed and value function estimation accuracy.
COST: Estimated 30,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 1.
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to improve the optimization performance by leveraging an efficient probabilistic model of the value function, but may require careful tuning of the model architecture and training procedure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Combining Parallelized Adaptive Sampling and Model-Based Optimization for Efficient Actor-Free Value Function Maximization
PROPOSAL: Combine the benefits of parallelized adaptive sampling and model-based optimization by using a learned probabilistic model to guide the adaptive sampling process. This would allow for efficient exploration of the search space while leveraging the compact and accurate representation of the value function provided by the model.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing actor-free methods and the revised proposal 3, focusing on both exploration-exploitation trade-offs and value function estimation accuracy.
COST: Estimated 40,000 GPU-hours on the same setup as proposal 1 (assuming a straightforward combination of proposals 1 and 5).
PREDICTION: This combined approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in actor-free value function maximization by leveraging the strengths of both parallelized adaptive sampling and model-based optimization, but may require careful tuning of the combined algorithm.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstrate Baselines for Offline Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of state-of-the-art video-language alignment models (e.g., CLIP, ALIGN) and step grounding models (e.g., ViPG, TEA) on a real-world dataset of instructional videos (e.g., Cooking 360) when trained and tested in an offline setting.
CONTROLS: Train each model from scratch on the Cooking 360 dataset, use a validation set for hyperparameter tuning, and compare their performance on a holdout test set.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: strong performance from CLIP and TEA, with potential for improvement with fine-tuning and data augmentation. Potential failure: ViPG might struggle due to its complex architecture and requirement for large amounts of data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigate the Performance of Large Pretrained Models on Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of several large, publicly available multimodal models (e.g., LLaMA, OPT, byT5) on a subset of the Cooking 360 dataset, focusing on zero-shot step grounding without any task-specific fine-tuning or adaptation.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of these models on a set of predefined steps from the Cooking 360 dataset, and contrast it with the performance of the baselines established in proposal 1. Additionally, probe the models' ability to zero-shot generalize to unseen steps and videos.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: strong zero-shot performance from some of the models, potentially similar to the best-performing offline models. Potential failure: OPT may struggle with egocentric procedural activity videos, as it is primarily designed for text-based tasks.

ACTION: REVISE

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Zero-Shot Performance on a Cooking Recipe Dataset
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the ability of off-the-shelf multimodal models (e.g. CLIP, DALL-E) to ground procedural steps in a dataset of cooking recipe videos (e.g. 1000+ videos from YouTube) without any task-specific training.
CONTROLS: We will keep the performance of three baseline models (a simple frame-caption similarity model, a state-of-the-art training-based VSG model, and a model-trained on a different yet related task, e.g. captioning recipe images) for comparison.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the off-the-shelf models to perform reasonably well (e.g. 50-60% accuracy on identifying steps in the video), with some variation depending on the model and dataset. Where they might struggle is in distinguishing between steps with similar appearances, such as the "adding spice" and "stirring" steps in a recipe.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning from Pseudo-Labeled Videos
PROPOSAL: We will take the knowledge gained from our zero-shot evaluation and fine-tune a pre-trained model (e.g. a version of CLIP pre-processed for VSG) on a pseudo-labeled dataset: a large collection of instructional videos (e.g. 10,000+ videos) that we can automatically pseudo-label using the procedures from our zero-shot experiment. We will aim to improve the model's performance on a given step of the video.
CONTROLS: We will compare the fine-tuned model to a model trained from scratch (and use techniques like early-stopped training and knowledge distillation to try and reduce overfitting).
COST: 200 GPU-hours (a relatively modest fine-tuning)
PREDICTION: We expect this method to improve the model's performance by 20-40% compared to the original zero-shot experiment, depending on the pseudo-labeling quality and the amount of fine-tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Refining the Zero-Shot Experiment
PROPOSAL: We will revise our zero-shot experiment to focus on specific datasets that control for the appearance and sequence of steps in a video, to more directly evaluate the model's ability to understand the semantic meaning of a step. For example, we can use a dataset of cooking videos where the same step is performed in different locations or with different objects, or use a dataset where the steps are interwoven with other distracting content.
CONTROLS: We will keep the original baseline models and use the same evaluation metrics as before, to facilitate comparison.
COST: no additional GPU hours (reusing previous data and evaluations)
PREDICTION: We expect the models to perform similarly to our original results, but with more nuanced comparisons possible due to the refined datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Online Video Step Grounding with Hindsight Gains
PROPOSAL: We will design a streaming algorithm that injects knowledge from past segments into the prediction for the current segment, without storing the whole history, by locally revising the decision with "hindsight gains": when a prediction made from the current segment is later confirmed (or refuted) by further video on the stream, we correct it and reuse the updated knowledge in the future predictions for that segment. We will evaluate this approach against a purely streaming baseline, which is the video step ground truth for each segment, and also try a variant that spreads the corrections over time to mitigate temporal noise.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the algorithm under various noise conditions (e.g. different segment lengths, added video noise, etc.) and compare the recall curve for our specifically trained baseline with that of hindsight-level corrected segment to baseline oversegmentatoin calibration  error světě

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Real-World Performance on Egocentric Procedural Activity Videos
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate our zero-shot and fine-tuned models on a real-world dataset of egocentric procedural activity videos (e.g. YouTube videos of people performing complex tasks like cooking or assembling furniture). We will use this evaluation to test the generalizability of our approach to more realistic and varied settings.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our models to a previously-developed egocentric activity recognition (EAR) baseline, and investigate whether any domain shifts occur.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (evaluating on a dataset with 5,000+ real-world egocentric activity videos and state of other the art  model s)
PREDICTION: We expect our models to perform well on the egocentric dataset, but to struggle with the more varied and nuanced procedural steps present in real-world examples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Temporal Resolution on Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: We will analyze the effect of temporal resolution (e.g. 25fps vs 60fps) on the performance of our models, by re-running our zero-shot and fine-tuned evaluations on subsets of the video datasets with varying resolutions. We will also explore whether our hindsight gains algorithm can mitigate the negative impact of lower temporal resolution on model performance.
CONTROLS: We will systematically vary the temporal resolution of the video inputs, and compare the performance of our models across different resolutions.
COST: 75 GPU-hours (evaluating on subsets of the video datasets)
PREDICTION: We expect the models to perform better with higher temporal resolution, but our hindsight gains algorithm to help close the gap between high-res and low-res performance.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Refining Real-World Evaluation with Human Judgement
PROPOSAL: We will revise our real-world evaluation setup to incorporate human judgments as an additional level of validation, by having human annotators review a subset of the model's predictions and provide their own ground truth labels for those steps. This will allow us to assess the accuracy of our models in real-world scenarios, and understand the effect of potential biases or limitations in the current automated labeling schemes.
CONTROLS: We will maintain the original EAR baseline for comparison, and use both automatic and human-labeled ground truth to evaluate model performance.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (annotator labor and data preparation)
PREDICTION: We expect the human judgments to provide a more nuanced understanding of the models' accuracy in real-world scenarios, and highlight potential areas for improvement in both model development and data annotation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Streaming Video Step Grounding System using Dual-Encoder Architecture
PROPOSAL: We propose a streaming video step grounding system that leverages a dual-encoder architecture, which consists of a visual encoder and a textual encoder. The visual encoder captures the visual content of the video, while the textual encoder encodes the step descriptions. We will use the Contrastive Learning framework to fine-tune the model on a streaming video step grounding task. We will experiment with the proposed system using a combination of real-world and synthetic datasets to evaluate its performance in different settings.
CONTROLS: We will compare the proposed system with the previously developed models (e.g., zero-shot and fine-tuned models) using various metrics, such as accuracy, precision, and recall.
COST: 250 GPU-hours (training and evaluating the dual-encoder architecture)
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed system to outperform the previous models by leveraging the strengths of both visual and textual encoders.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Online Video Step Grounding with Sampling Strategies
PROPOSAL: We will design and evaluate several sampling strategies for online video step grounding, aiming to improve the efficiency of the hindsight gains algorithm while maintaining or improving its accuracy. The strategies will focus on reducing the number of past segments to consider, for example, by only retaining segments that are most relevant to the current step or by using uncertainty estimates to prioritize segments with more informative information.
CONTROLS: We will compare the sampling strategies with baseline and hindsight gains algorithms using various metrics such as accuracy, efficiency, and memory requirements.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (evaluating sampling strategies and fine-tuning the algorithm)
PREDICTION: We expect the sampling strategies to significantly improve the efficiency of the hindsight gains algorithm, reducing memory requirements and computation time, while maintaining or slightly improving its accuracy in real-world settings.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: Refining the Dual-Encoder Streaming Video Step Grounding System
PROPOSAL: We will revise the streaming video step grounding system using the dual-encoder architecture to incorporate the efficient online video step grounding with sampling strategies, aiming to further improve its accuracy, efficiency, and robustness in real-world settings. We will also explore using transfer learning from pseudo-labeled videos to improve the system's performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare the revised system with the previous models using various metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, and efficiency.
COST: 120 GPU-hours (fine-tuning and evaluating the revised system)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised system to achieve state-of-the-art performance on streaming video step grounding tasks, with improved efficiency and robustness.

We will analyze the effect of temporal resolution (e.g. 25fps vs 60fps) on the performance of our models, by re-running our zero-shot and fine-tuned evaluations on subsets of the video datasets with varying resolutions. We will revise the streaming video step grounding system using the dual-encoder architecture to incorporate the efficient online video step grounding with sampling strategies, aiming to further improve its accuracy, efficiency, and robustness in real-world settings. TITLE:  Efficient Memory-Augmented Online Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL:  We design a memory-augmented architecture that leverages a neural module for capturing long-term dependencies in the sequence of video segments. Our model infers salient and task-relevant information from the history of video segments and stores it in an external memory. This, in turn, enhances temporal filtering and decision-making on the current video segment, without requiring explicit storage of previous information. We evaluate the model on both  the VIST-Grounding for Procedural Step Grounding (PSG) and Procedural Step Grounding Dataset (StepGrounded-V1.0) with several variations of architectures to optimize memory size, granularity, and inference speed. Additionally, we implement inter-instance consistency by enriching the memory using non-local and inter-frame relationships, thereby increasing information propagation.
