We also propose a task-agnostic attention mechanism to selectively focus on the most relevant tasks and domains during inference. Our experiments demonstrate that MTL-VSG outperforms state-of-the-art methods on a range of video grounding benchmarks and significantly improves transferability across tasks and domains.
propositions.titre: Online Video Step Grounding with Multi-Task Learning for Transferability

propositions.controles: We compare EXO-VSG with our previous methods and a variant that uses a single-source knowledge approach.
propositions.texte: We propose a novel approach that incorporates exogenous knowledge from external sources, such as text descriptions, enrolment information, and  worker certifications to enhance the robustness of our online video step grounding model. Our approach, dubbed EXO-VSG, uses a cross-modal fusion mechanism to combine the exogenous knowledge with the video embeddings, allowing the model to learn more robust and accurate representations. We also propose a contextualized loss function to adapt the model to different exogenous knowledge sources and imbalances in the data. Our experiments demonstrate that EXO-VSG significantly improves the robustness and accuracy of online video step grounding.
propositions.titre: Online Video Step Grounding with Exogenous Knowledge for Enhanced Robustness

propositions.controles: We compare EDBG-VSG with our previous methods and a variant that uses a single-explainability approach.
propositions.texte: We propose an explainability and debugging framework for online video step grounding that provides insights into the model's decision-making process and identifies potential errors. Our approach, dubbed EDBG-VSG, uses a combination of attention-based visualization, saliency maps, and input gradients to provide explanations for the model's predictions. We also develop a debugging framework that identifies potential errors in the model's decision-making process and provides suggestions for improvement. Our experiments demonstrate that EDBG-VSG significantly improves the trustworthiness and usability of online video step grounding in real-world applications.
propositions.titre: Online Video Step Grounding with Explainability and Debugging for Real-World Applications

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: بازlines for Single-Forward-Pass AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: We compare the standard AlphaFold3 architecture with a baseline that uses a single forward pass by replacing the iterative diffusion sampler with a fixed-point iteration-based alternative, which achieves a similar level of accuracy on shorter sequences by deterministically computing the iterative process. Specifically, we use a fixed-point iteration that appends additional noise and refines the sequence in a predetermined number of steps, similar to the conventional iterative diffusion approach but without the multiple calls to the diffusion model. We expect this baseline to closely match AlphaFold3's performance on shorter sequences but struggle on longer sequences, where the predictive signal weakens significantly due to the fixed-point iteration's lack of adaptability.
CONTROLS: Original AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: For shorter protein sequences (<500 amino acids), the single forward pass AlphaFold3 will be very close to the iterative version. However, on longer sequences (>1000 amino acids), it might start to suffer due to its inability to adapt to changing signal quality, which could be exacerbated by the use of fixed-point iteration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Low-Rank Asymptotic Behavior of AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: To establish a theoretical foundation for accelerating the diffusion process, we investigate the low-rank asymptotic behavior of AlphaFold3's iterated solutions using techniques from linear algebra and dynamical systems theory, specifically the analysis of Lyapunov exponents. This will help us understand the speed and stability of convergence in the diffusion process and how it is affected by sequence length. Specifically, we will compute and analyze the eigenvalues of the diffusion matrix for representative sequence lengths and protein types, expecting that a low-rank structure emerges at the longer sequence lengths where acceleration methods become most relevant.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging principles from dynamical systems, we anticipate discovering a regular low-rank asymptotic structure of the iterated solutions of AlphaFold3, supporting the idea that acceleration can be achieved by vectorized operations on rank-constrained matrices.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Low-Rank Asymptotic Behavior of AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: (Revised version) To establish a theoretical foundation for accelerating the diffusion process, we investigate the low-rank asymptotic behavior of the solution manifold of AlphaFold3's iterated diffusion process using techniques from differential geometry and topological data analysis. By assuming an underlying low-rank structure (based on the results from our previous theoretical investigations), we will analyze its implications for the convergence properties of the diffusion process, specifically whether low-rank constraints can be used to provably accelerate or improve the stability of the iterations for longer sequence lengths. A key aspect of our analysis will be to relate these theoretical insights to the experimental findings obtained from testing accelerated low-rank diffusion schemes on real-world protein sequence datasets.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler and accelerated low-rank diffusion scheme.
COST: 75 GPU-hours initially for analysis, possibly more for experimental validation
PREDICTION: Our results should demonstrate that by enforcing low-rank constraints in the diffusion process, we can effectively accelerate or stabilize its behavior, supporting our hypothesis that low-rank solutions can improve computational efficiency without sacrificing predictive fidelity.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Investigating Low-Rank Asymptotic Behavior of AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: (Revised version) To establish a theoretical foundation for accelerating the diffusion process, we investigate the low-rank asymptotic behavior of the solution manifold of AlphaFold3's iterated diffusion process using techniques from differential geometry and topological data analysis. By assuming an underlying low-rank structure and employing matrix manifold optimization methods, we will analyze its implications for the convergence properties of the diffusion process, specifically whether low-rank constraints can be used to provably accelerate or improve the stability of the iterations for longer sequence lengths.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler and low-rank constrained optimization.
COST: 75 GPU-hours initially for analysis, possibly more for experimental validation
PREDICTION: Our results should demonstrate that by enforcing low-rank constraints in the diffusion process, we can effectively accelerate or stabilize its behavior, supporting our hypothesis that low-rank solutions can improve computational efficiency without sacrificing predictive fidelity. 

Note: the new version of the revision involves using low-rank constrained optimization, which was not present in the original proposal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Consistency Regularization for AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: To adapt consistency regularization to AlphaFold3's architecture, we propose a novel, unified approach that leverages the relationship between the diffused states and the canonical values in a sequence-dependent manner. Specifically, we introduce a consistency loss term that measures the difference between the current state and the expected canonical state at each iteration, conditioned on the sequence length. This ensures that the sequence-specific geometry is maintained, while also accommodating the variable-length properties of proteins. We expect that this adaptive consistency regularization will help to stabilize the iterative process, reducing the likelihood of divergence on longer sequences.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler and fixed-script consistency regularization for comparison.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging sequence-dependent consistency regularization, we anticipate improving the stability and reliability of the iterative diffusion process, which should benefit the overall performance and usability of the accelerated model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-parallel Consistency Regularization for AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: To further adapt consistency regularization to AlphaFold3's architecture, we propose a gradient-parallel consistency loss term, which measures the difference between the gradient of the diffused states with respect to sequence positions and the expected canonical gradient. This term ensures that the sequence-specific geometry is maintained, while also respecting the gradients of each position in the sequence. We expect that this gradient-parallel consistency regularization will help to further stabilize the iterative process, reducing the likelihood of divergence on longer sequences.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler, unified consistency regularization, and gradient-parallel consistency regularization for comparison.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging gradient-parallel consistency regularization, we anticipate additional improvements in the stability and reliability of the iterative diffusion process, particularly on longer sequences, resulting in enhanced overall performance and usability of the accelerated model.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Unified Consistency Regularization for AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: (Revised version) To further adapt consistency regularization to AlphaFold3's architecture, we propose a unified consistency loss term that combines both the diffused state and the gradient of the diffused states with respect to sequence positions. Specifically, we use an ensemble of pre-trained models, each trained with a different type of consistency loss (state-dependent and gradient-dependent), and create a weighted ensemble that balances the contributions of both types. We expect that this unified approach will provide a solid compromise between maintaining sequence-specific geometry and respecting the gradients of each position in the sequence.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler and a combination of unified and gradient-parallel consistency regularization.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging the unified consistency loss term, we anticipate improving the stability and reliability of the iterative diffusion process, while maintaining the benefits of both state-dependent and gradient-dependent consistency losses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Accelerating AlphaFold3 with Vectorized Low-Rank Diffusion
PROPOSAL: To further accelerate the diffusion process, we propose a novel vectorized low-rank diffusion scheme that exploits the low-rank structure of the diffusion matrix. Specifically, we use a combination of low-rank matrix approximation and vectorized operations to accelerate the diffusion process, while maintaining the accuracy of the original diffusion process. We expect that this approach will provide a significant speedup, especially on longer sequences, by reducing the computational cost of the diffusion process.
CONTROLS: Standard AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler, vectorized low-rank diffusion scheme, and a combination of unified and gradient-parallel consistency regularization.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging the vectorized low-rank diffusion scheme, we anticipate achieving a significant speedup of the diffusion process, particularly on longer sequences, while maintaining the accuracy and stability of the original diffusion process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Evaluation of Accelerated AlphaFold3 on Protein Binder Design
PROPOSAL: To demonstrate the practical utility of the accelerated AlphaFold3 model, we evaluate its performance on protein binder design, a critical application in biotechnology and pharmaceuticals. We use a large real-world dataset of protein-ligand complexes and compare the performance of the accelerated model with that of the original AlphaFold3 model on metrics such as binding affinity prediction and protein-ligand pose prediction. We expect that the accelerated model will show equivalent or improved performance while being significantly faster.
CONTROLS: Original AlphaFold3 model with iterative diffusion sampler, accelerated AlphaFold3 model with vectorized low-rank diffusion scheme and unified consistency regularization, and a large real-world protein-ligand dataset.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging the accelerated AlphaFold3 model, we anticipate achieving state-of-the-art performance on protein binder design while reducing the computational time and cost associated with protein structure prediction, making it a highly competitive solution for industrial applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalability and Reproducibility Evaluation of Accelerated AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: To ensure the reproducibility and scalability of the accelerated AlphaFold3 model, we evaluate its performance on hardware configurations with varying numbers of GPUs and different architectures, as well as its performance on a range of real-world protein sequences with varying lengths. We also provide recommendations for hyperparameter tuning and optimization to ensure that the model can be easily adapted for use in industrial settings. We expect that the accelerated model will demonstrate robustness and reproducibility across different hardware configurations and sequence lengths.
CONTROLS: Reproducibility and scalability evaluation using a range of protein sequences with varying lengths and on different hardware configurations.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging the accelerated AlphaFold3 model, we anticipate achieving a comprehensive evaluation of its scalability and reproducibility, ensuring that it can be widely adopted in industrial settings for protein structure prediction and design.

TITLE: Simplifying Consistency Schedules for Protein Sequence Lengths
PROPOSAL: Adapt high-order consistency models to variable protein sequence lengths by employing a dynamic step scheduling strategy. We propose learning the step size from the data, with an input-dependent step size that adjusts based on the sequence length and a fixed maximum step size.
CONTROLS: Compare dynamic scheduling to conventional constant step size schedules on several datasets, including PDBBind and Protein-ligand complexes from Rose Luo dataset, while measuring training stability and predictive accuracy.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (20K iterations on a single RTX A6000 with batch size 32)
PREDICTION: Expected result is improved training stability and slightly reduced accuracy compared to conventional schedules, with potential for further improvement with ensembling or stage-wise instructional consistency. actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Recycling Iterations on AlphaFold3's Accuracy and Efficiency
PROPOSAL:  Implement a range of recycling iteration schedules for AlphaFold3 on protein, protein-ligand, and nucleic-acid complexes, varying from the original multi-step diffusion to a single recursive pass, and measure their respective accuracy and efficiency using metrics such as RMSD, MSE, and execution time.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original AlphaFold3 and the alpha version of AlphaFold2 to establish a baseline for efficacy and efficiency.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that significantly reducing the number of recycling iterations will result in a substantial decrease in the model's predictive accuracy, but by employing advanced diffusion-based techniques to accelerate the diffusion process, we can potentially balance the efficiency cost and accuracy trade-off. However, we expect degradation in results for long sequences.

Some expected failures: high-molecular weight complexes being poor the where we use the iterations with regard to assessing.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Consistency Models for Accelerating the Iterative Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: Design and implement consistency models specifically tailored to the AlphaFold3 architecture, aiming to learn a consistent representation of molecular structures during the iterative diffusion process. This could involve modifying the Pairformer trunk to incorporate consistency penalties or using an external consistency network to steer the diffusion process.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of consistency models trained on different sequence lengths and molecular complexity levels to establish the most effective approach, and ablate the consistency module to assess its importance.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see substantial improvements in efficiency when employing the consistency models, particularly for longer sequences, and reasonable assurance that the accuracy would be retrievable on the longer-range. One failure mode includes suboptimal adjustments in the consistency calculation method could cause model inaccuracies and eventually could activate destabilizing impact zones.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Consistency Models for Accelerating the Iterative Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: Revising the proposal to incorporate variable-step consistency, allowing the consistency models to adjust their timestep based on the sequence length and molecular complexity, preventing potential distribution shifts on long sequences and providing a more stable learning signal on short sequences. This will be achieved by adaptively adjusting the E steps in the geometry step, and differentiating the time step along it according to consistency loss value derivative. 
CONTROLS: Compare against previous consistency model results and ablate variable-step consistency to assess its importance.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect this refinement to improve model stability and efficiency on long sequences, reducing potential instabilities and hallucinations, but may still encounter limitations when dealing with very complex systems or near the physical limits of molecule mass.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Lightweight Hierarchical Attention for Pairformer-Based Molecular Modeling
PROPOSAL: Introduce a lightweight hierarchical attention mechanism into the Pairformer trunk, allowing the model to selectively focus on the most relevant regions of the molecule, thus reducing the computational overhead and potentially preserving predictive accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the modified Pairformer with the original architecture, and ablate different aspects of the hierarchical attention mechanism to assess its importance.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the lightweight hierarchical attention will significantly reduce the computational requirements without compromising the overall accuracy of the model, potentially providing an efficient trade-off between execution time and structure quality. We note that this proposal may encounter difficulties with potentially weak features which could be more uncertain about.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Lightweight Hierarchical Attention for Pairformer-Based Molecular Modeling
PROPOSAL: Renaming the hierarchical attention mechanism to the "Region-Attention" mechanism, emphasizing its explicit focus on identifying the most relevant regions of the molecule based on the preprocessed sequence-induced pair features. We will investigate two different region-attention schemes: one based on fixed windows and the other on a dynamic regional splitting based solely on pair energy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of both region-attention mechanisms with the original Pairformer, and analyze the effect of adjusting the window size and splitting threshold on the region-attention mechanism.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours (addition of 300 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: We expect the Region-Attention mechanism to further improve the efficiency of the Pairformer, especially for longer sequences, while also providing a reasonable balance between computational requirements and structure quality.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Directional Graph Transformer for Modeling Molecular Conformation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a directional graph transformer module that focuses on modeling the spatial relationships between atoms in the molecule, allowing the model to better capture the 3D structure and geometric constraints. This will be achieved by representing the molecule as a directed graph, where each edge encodes the directional relationship between the corresponding atoms.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the directional graph transformer with the original AlphaFold3 architecture, and ablate different components to assess their importance.
COST: 2200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the directional graph transformer to provide significant improvements in modeling molecular conformation, especially for larger and more complex molecules, and reduce the reliance on iterative diffusion for maintaining geometric constraints. This proposal may require careful adjustments in model hyperparameters to ensure stable training and avoid plateaus or overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Consistency Models for Accelerating the Iterative Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: Revising the consistency model training procedure to use a curriculum learning approach, where the training process starts with simple molecular structures and gradually moves on to more complex ones, providing the model with a more stable learning signal and improving its robustness to different sequence lengths.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the updated consistency model with the original consistency model, and analyze the effect of different curriculum learning strategies on the model's performance.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours (update of existing project)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised consistency model to improve the model's ability to generalize across different molecular structures and sequence lengths, and reduce the frequency of instability and hallucinations. This approach may require careful tuning of the curriculum learning schedule to optimize the model's performance.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Accelerated Denoising Diffusion Model for Protein Structure Prediction
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel denoising diffusion model specifically designed for protein structure prediction, which leverages the strengths of the directional graph transformer and consistency models to efficiently model the probabilistic distributions of molecular conformations. This model will use a noise schedule adapted to protein sequences and incorporate a learnable denoising process to further reduce computational overhead.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the accelerated denoising diffusion model with the original AlphaFold3 architecture, and ablate different components to assess their importance.
COST: 3500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the accelerated denoising diffusion model to provide significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency, enabling fast and reliable protein structure prediction on a wide range of sequence lengths and complexities. However, this proposal may require careful tuning of the model's hyperparameters to ensure stable training and avoid overfitting to a particular class of molecules.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Recycling Iterations on AlphaFold3's Accuracy and Efficiency
PROPOSAL: Revising the proposal to incorporate results from the other accelerated models, and comparing the performance of the original AlphaFold3 with the accelerated models from proposals 2-5. This will provide a comprehensive understanding of the trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and model complexity for different accelerated approaches.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the accelerated models with the original AlphaFold3, and analyze the effect of different accelerated components on the model's performance.
COST: 0 additional GPU-hours (utilizing existing projects)
PREDICTION: We expect this revised proposal to provide valuable insights into the optimal accelerated approach for protein structure prediction, considering the strengths and weaknesses of each accelerated model. This will inform the development of a highly efficient and accurate protein structure prediction framework.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Unified Accelerated AlphaFold3 Framework (UAAF)
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework that combines the accelerated approaches from proposals 2-5 into a single, modular framework. This framework will enable researchers and practitioners to easily experiment with different accelerated components and hyperparameter settings, facilitating the discovery of optimal accelerated configurations for protein structure prediction.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of different accelerated configurations within the UAAF framework, and evaluate the framework's modularity and ease of use.
COST: 5000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the UAAF framework to become a widely adopted standard for accelerated protein structure prediction, enabling the efficient prediction of high-quality protein structures for a wide range of applications. This framework will also facilitate the discovery of new accelerated approaches and the evaluation of their performance.

propositions.prediction: We expect the Region-Attention mechanism to further improve the efficiency of the Pairformer, especially for longer sequences, while also providing a reasonable balance between computational requirements and structure quality.
propositions.texte: Renaming the hierarchical attention mechanism to the "Region-Attention" mechanism, emphasizing its explicit focus on identifying the most relevant regions of the molecule based on the preprocessed sequence-induced pair features. We will investigate two different region-attention schemes: one based on fixed windows and the other on a dynamic regional splitting based solely on pair energy.
propositions.titre: Lightweight Hierarchical Attention for Pairformer-Based Molecular Modeling

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of the directional graph transformer with the original AlphaFold3 architecture, and ablate different components to assess their importance.
propositions.prediction: We expect the directional graph transformer to provide significant improvements in modeling molecular conformation, especially for larger and more complex molecules, and reduce the reliance on iterative diffusion for maintaining geometric constraints. This proposal may require careful adjustments in model hyperparameters to ensure stable training and avoid plateaus or overfitting.
propositions.texte: Introduce a directional graph transformer module that focuses on modeling the spatial relationships between atoms in the molecule, allowing the model to better capture the 3D structure and geometric constraints. This will be achieved by representing the molecule as a directed graph, where each edge encodes the directional relationship between the corresponding atoms.
propositions.titre: Directional Graph Transformer for Modeling Molecular Conformation

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of the accelerated denoising diffusion model with the original AlphaFold3 architecture, and ablate different components to assess their importance.
propositions.prediction: We expect the accelerated denoising diffusion model to provide significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency, enabling fast and reliable protein structure prediction on a wide range of sequence lengths and complexities. However, this proposal may require careful tuning of the model's hyperparameters to ensure stable training and avoid overfitting to a particular class of molecules.
propositions.texte: Introduce a novel denoising diffusion model specifically designed for protein structure prediction, which leverages the strengths of the directional graph transformer and consistency models to efficiently model the probabilistic distributions of molecular conformations. This model will use a noise schedule adapted to protein sequences and incorporate a learnable denoising process to further reduce computational overhead.
propositions.titre: Accelerated Denoising Diffusion Model for Protein Structure Prediction

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of different accelerated configurations within the UAAF framework, and evaluate the framework's modularity and ease of use.
propositions.prediction: We expect the UAAF framework to become a widely adopted standard for accelerated protein structure prediction, enabling the efficient prediction of high-quality protein structures for a wide range of applications. This framework will also facilitate the discovery of new accelerated approaches and the evaluation of their performance.
propositions.texte: Develop a unified framework that combines the accelerated approaches from proposals 2-5 into a single, modular framework. This framework will enable researchers and practitioners to easily experiment with different accelerated components and hyperparameter settings, facilitating the discovery of optimal accelerated configurations for protein structure prediction.
propositions.titre: Unified Accelerated AlphaFold3 Framework (UAAF)

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating alternating gradient flows for one-step discrete generators
PROPOSAL: Revise the forward pass of the discrete generator by storing an auxiliary state that represents the information encoded in the input data (e.g., a batch of class labels or image directions), and use this auxiliary state to compute a separate, "adversarial" loss that is added to the standard reconstruction loss. The auxiliary state is then updated on the backwards pass via an additional gradient backpropagation step that is separate from the standard reconstruction loss. This is similar to how alternating gradient flows are used in GAN training, but adapted for discrete generators and to allow for gradient passing through the tokenizer.
CONTROLS: Train a discrete generator with the proposed alternating gradient flows and compare it to a baseline generator trained with standard reconstruction loss alone. As a control, also train a generator using a straight-through estimator with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with alternating gradient flows to achieve lower reconstruction loss and better downstream task performance compared to the baseline, while also reducing the high variance in the gradients from the Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. However, it may require careful tuning of the auxiliary state and adversarial loss to achieve convergence and stable training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous relaxation of discrete tokens via sparse linear programming
PROPOSAL: Use a sparse linear programming (LP) relaxation of the discrete token space, where each token is represented as a sparse combination of continuous basis vectors. This relaxation can be used as an objective function in the generator's loss function, allowing for gradient-based optimization of the generator's parameters with respect to the relaxed continuous metric. Specifically, we can use an efficient LP solver to relaxation of the discrete token assignment problem, allowing for gradients to flow through the generator while maintaining a lower-bound on the discrete metric.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed LP relaxation to standard Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and a baseline generator trained with standard reconstruction loss. As a control, also train a generator using a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) relaxation of the discrete token space.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the LP-relaxed generator to achieve lower reconstruction loss and better downstream task performance compared to the Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, while also reducing the high computational overhead of the MILP relaxation. However, it may require careful tuning of the LP parameters to achieve convergence and stable training.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Theory of the alternating gradient flows for one-step discrete generators
PROPOSAL: Theoretically analyze the alternating gradient flows for one-step discrete generators, proving that the additional gradient backpropagation step allows for the gradients from the auxiliary state to be correctly aligned with the reconstruction loss in the generator's parameters. This results in a lower-variance estimate of the reconstruction loss and allows for more efficient training of the generator. We will also derive an expression for the variance of the estimated reconstruction loss and analyze the trade-off between the benefits of the alternating gradient flows and the increased computational overhead.
CONTROLS: None required
COST: 0 GPU-hours (theoretical analysis only)
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis will provide a foundation for understanding the behavior of the alternating gradient flows and will provide insights into how to design the auxiliary state and adversarial loss for efficient training. Although the theory will not have a direct impact on the performance of the generator, it will improve our understanding of the underlying mechanisms and will provide a framework for future experiments and analyses.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 1
TITLE: Investigating alternating gradient flows for one-step discrete generators with a novel auxiliary state
PROPOSAL: Revise the auxiliary state used in the alternating gradient flows by incorporating a Learnable Class Conditional (LCC) embedding space, which is learned during training and is conditioned on the input class labels. The LCC embedding space provides a richer representation of the class semantics and allows the generator to better align with the downstream task objectives. The gradients from the LCC embedding space are then combined with the reconstruction loss to regularize the generator's parameters.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed LCC embedding space to a baseline with a fixed class embedding space (e.g. learned from a pre-trained model).
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with the LCC embedding space to achieve better downstream task performance and more accurate class-conditioned generation compared to the baseline, while also improving the stability and convergence of the alternating gradient flows training process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-end differentiable reward optimization for one-step discrete generators
PROPOSAL: To allow for the gradients from downstream reward models to pass through the tokenizer and affect the generator's parameters, we use the "Reweighter" (RW) as an intermediate proxy. The RW applies a learnable reweighting function to the decoded image and provides a continuous reward signal that can be backpropagated through the generator. We will develop and compare different reweighting functions and incorporate the proposed RW into the existing one-step discrete generator.
CONTROLS: Compare the RW to a baseline with direct use of the reward model's gradients on the decoded image, as well as to a baseline with a fixed reweighting function (e.g., an identity function).
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with the RW to achieve better downstream task performance and more accurate reward-based optimization compared to the baseline, while also providing a more flexible and interpretable way to incorporate user preferences and reward signals into the training process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-modal one-step discrete generators for text-to-image synthesis
PROPOSAL: To extend the one-step discrete generator to multi-modal tasks, such as text-to-image synthesis with varying image styles or complex scene descriptions, we propose a adaptive-modal attention mechanism that can dynamically adjust the relevance of different text and image features according to the specific generation task. This mechanism enables the generator to capture complex correlations between text and image and produce diverse, high-quality images for various input text prompts.
CONTROLS: Compare the adaptive-modal attention mechanism to a baseline with fixed attention weights, as well as to a baseline with a attention-free generator.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with adaptive-modal attention mechanism to achieve better multi-modal generation performance, including more diverse and high-quality images for complex text prompts, while also maintaining the benefits of the one-step discrete generator in terms of efficiency and stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-aware training for one-step discrete generators
PROPOSAL: To improve the precision and robustness of the one-step discrete generator, we propose a quantization-aware training approach that simultaneously optimizes the generator's parameters and the quantization levels of the discrete tokens. This approach allows us to learn optimal discrete representations and representations that are robust to discretization errors, resulting in better generation quality and reduced over-quantization artifacts.
CONTROLS: Compare the quantization-aware training to a baseline with standard discrete token representation, as well as to a baseline with post-training quantization.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with quantization-aware training to produce better image quality and fewer quantization artifacts compared to the baseline, while also maintaining the efficiency benefits of the one-step discrete generator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical neural transfer learning for bridging teacher-student discrete generators
PROPOSAL: To bridge the performance gap between the teacher and the student discrete generators, we propose a hierarchical neural transfer learning approach that learns task-agnostic and task-specific knowledge from the teacher generator and adapts it to the student generator. This approach enables the student generator to learn from the teacher's imperfections and adapt to the target distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare the hierarchical neural transfer learning to a baseline with direct distillation, as well as to a baseline with random initialization.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the student generator with hierarchical neural transfer learning to achieve better performance and faster convergence compared to the baseline, while also maintaining the benefits of the one-step discrete generator in terms of efficiency and stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial training for discrete latent space refinement
PROPOSAL: To improve the quality and realism of the generated images, we propose an adversarial training approach that refines the discrete latent space of the one-step discrete generator. This involves training a discriminator that distinguishes between the generated images and real images, and using the generated images as input to the generator to refine its latent space.
CONTROLS: Compare the adversarial training to a baseline with standard reconstruction loss, as well as to a baseline with random sampling from the latent space.
COST: 280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator with adversarial training to produce more realistic and diverse generated images compared to the baseline, while also maintaining the benefits of the one-step discrete generator in terms of efficiency and stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:Unified architecture for one-step discrete generation: a benchmarking study
PROPOSAL: To provide a comprehensive comparison of the various one-step discrete generation methods, we propose a unified architecture that integrates the methods from previous proposals (1-7) and a benchmarking study to evaluate their performance on a range of tasks, including image synthesis, image-to-image translation, and text-to-image synthesis. This will help identify the strengths and weaknesses of each method and provide insights for future research directions.
CONTROLS: Compare the unified architecture to a baseline with standard discrete token representation, as well as to individual models from previous proposals.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the unified architecture to provide a comprehensive comparison of the state-of-the-art one-step discrete generation methods and help identify the most effective methods for specific tasks and applications.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Flow via Intermediate Representations
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of intermediate representations to bypass the gradient-blocking problem in one-step discrete generators. Specifically, we propose to pre-train a proxy model that predicts the discrete token outputs of the one-step generator, enabling the differentiation of the response model's inputs that are conditioned on the proxy's outputs. We aim to align the proxy with the target distribution and utilize this match to improve gradient flow.
CONTROLS: We compare against a baseline where gradients are computed directly from the discrete generator's outputs. We also evaluate the performance of the proxy model trained on different datasets and with varying levels of training resources.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (the proxy model requires an initial pre-training, followed by finetuning for aligning with the teacher and the downstream objectives).
PREDICTION: This intermediate representation can alleviate the gradient-blocking issue and allow for efficient end-to-end optimization. However, we could fail if the proxy model's alignment becomes too loose during the fine-tuning process, or if the proxy itself becomes a bottleneck in computation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Relaxation of Discrete Tokens
PROPOSAL: We explore adaptive relaxation methods that balance gradient stability and low-variance, by adjusting the smoothness of the intermediate representation based on the complexity of the downstream objective and changes in the student's optimization trajectory. Specifically, we extend the original soft-argmax method to incorporate a learned, adaptive control over the level of relaxation, thus trading-off between bias and variance under the guidance of the current optimization state.
CONTROLS: We compare against both non-relaxation approaches (proposal 1) and variable scope relaxation (e.g., that treats some tokens but not others as if they are soft). Additionally, we investigate whether adaptive relaxation reduces overfitting or boosts performance by comparing against models without it or with a fixed relaxation level.
COST: 500 GPU-hours, as we can adaptively relax a model pre-trained with proposal 1 and finetune on downstream objectives.
PREDICTION: Adaptive relaxation allows us to efficiently apply gradient-based training to one-step discrete generators with non-trivial downstream objectives without relying on non-continuous interleaving strategies. However, adapting to more complex objectives or non-stationary students may require more sophisticated approaches to prevent over-smoothing.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Gradient Flow via Concatenated Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We modify proposal 1 to use concatenated embeddings instead of an intermediate representation. We pre-train a sequence of embedding layers that concate sequentially the student's input, a static token representation of the teacher's outputs, and finally a predict-next token given input, but written as Location embedding in proposal 1 that to inversely output location wise teacher token. This concatenated sequence aligns with the target distribution and provides a differentiable way for backpropagating gradients from downstream objectives through the discrete generator.
CONTROLS: We maintain the same controls as before, but also remove the proxy model's retraining, enabling a faster comparison to existing state-of-the-art models.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (less than proposal 1 due to concatenation's smaller footprint and parallelizable pre-training).
PREDICTION: Unlike the intermediate model, the concatenated embeddings directly align with the target distribution without added layers, potentially reducing modeling errors. Additionally, compared to adaptive relaxation methods, we find that some concatenations have lower variance and gradient fluctuations at multiple discrete sampling steps.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Gradient Flow via Concatenated Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We modify the intermediate representation from proposal 1 to use concatenated embeddings. We pre-train a sequence of embedding layers that concate sequentially the student's input, a static token representation of the teacher's outputs, and finally a predict-next token given input. This concatenated sequence aligns with the target distribution and provides a differentiable way for backpropagating gradients from downstream objectives through the discrete generator.
CONTROLS: We compare against a baseline where gradients are computed directly from the discrete generator's outputs, and also maintain the evaluation of the proxy model trained on different datasets and with varying levels of training resources.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (less than original proposal due to concatenation's smaller footprint and parallelizable pre-training).
PREDICTION: In contrast to the original intermediate representation, the concatenated embeddings directly align with the target distribution without added layers, potentially reducing modeling errors. However, we must investigate whether the concatenated sequence is over-fitting to the pre-trained teacher, affecting its ability to capture the current student's distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Aware Gradient Propagation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel variant of reward-aware optimization that focuses on stabilizing the gradient flow through the discrete generator. Specifically, we use the output of the teacher's decoder as a guiding signal to augment the reward model during training, helping the student's gradients to stay aligned with the target distribution and improving overall performance on downstream objectives. We propose a soft-weighted reward scheme that progressively incorporates the teacher's output into the student's optimization process.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the effectiveness of our reward-aware gradient propagation approach by deploying it in conjunction with both concatenated embeddings and adaptive relaxation methods and comparing against the baseline where gradients are computed directly from the discrete generator's outputs.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours, mainly due to augmenting the existing optimization procedures with additional forward and backward passes through the teacher's decoder to incorporate the reward scheme.
PREDICTION: Reward-aware gradient propagation can significantly enhance the quality of the student's output and guide its optimization process towards more effective alignment with downstream objectives, ultimately boosting performance on one-step discrete generators. However, we must carefully monitor the balance between the teacher's guiding signal and the student's current optimization trajectory to avoid over-reliance on the former and maintain stability in training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offloading Teacher-Specific Modeling Errors
PROPOSAL: We introduce a technique that decomposes the teacher model into two separate components: a distribution-aware component that captures the teacher's alignments with the target distribution, and a task-specific component responsible for modeling downstream objectives. We then fine-tune the distribution-aware component separately, allowing it to relearn the teacher's representation under the guidance of the student's optimization process, while minimizing the task-specific component's influence on gradient computation.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed method against the standard distillation setting, training the full teacher model or only the task-specific component, and evaluate its effectiveness on the downstream objectives using both random and task-specific teacher student combinations.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours, as the offloading and separate fine-tuning approach only add a linear overhead to the initial distillation training.
PREDICTION: This approach should reduce the impact of teacher-specific modeling errors on student optimization by focusing on the teacher's alignment with the target distribution and realigning it with the student's current model. However, we must carefully consider how the level of decomposition affects the teacher's remaining task-specific knowledge and overall training stability.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Adaptive Relaxation of Discrete Tokens
PROPOSAL: We incorporate offloading teacher-specific modeling errors into adaptive relaxation methods. actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Flow Through the Teacher-Student Pipeline
PROPOSAL: Revise the teacher-student distillation framework to allow for gradient flow through the discrete student generator by using a differentiable token relaxation, such as the Gumbel-softmax, in conjunction with a straight-through estimator. Specifically, at each step, the student's output will use the relaxed token distributions, but pass through the original discrete token output during backpropagation.
CONTROLS: Compare against both on-policy Di[M]O and a baseline that uses the usual non-differentiable sampling.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours for a large-scale evaluation on text-to-image generation, estimated based on 1000 pre-distillation iterations and a batch size of 32.
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more efficient gradient-based training of the student, but might still suffer from biases and numerical instabilities due to the relaxed token distributions, which could lead to slow convergence or suboptimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Differentiable Reward Tuning with Representative Samples
PROPOSAL: To address the second question and let post-distillation refinements correct the errors inherited from the teacher, develop a method that uses representative samples from the token decoder to compute gradients that can flow back to the student. The representative samples are selected using a learned selector network that minimizes the difference between the selector's output and the token decoder's output. This approach will enable the student to fine-tune for downstream objectives such as aesthetic quality and prompt-following.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the method on text-to-image generation and image synthesis tasks, comparing against a baseline that uses the entire token decoder output for gradient computation. Also, study the impact of different selector network architectures on the quality of the representative samples.
COST: Estimated 3000 GPU-hours for a text-to-image generation task with a batch size of 128 and 5000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The approach has the potential to improve the quality of the generated images and prompt-following abilities, but its effectiveness will depend on the design of the selector network and the quality of the representative samples selected.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Gradient Flow Through the Teacher-Student Pipeline (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal from Turn 1 to use a combination of the Gumbel-softmax relaxation and the straight-through estimator, but with an additional adaptation step to improve the teacher's alignment with downstream objectives. The adaptation step will use a learned reward model to fine-tune the teacher's output for specific objectives such as aesthetic quality, and then distill the adapted teacher into the student using the revised pipeline.
CONTROLS: Compare against both the original on-policy Di[M]O and the baseline that uses the usual non-differentiable sampling, as well as against the original teacher-student pipeline without adaptation (to study the impact of the adaptation step).
COST: Estimated 1500 GPU-hours for a text-to-image generation task with a batch size of 64 and 2000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The revised approach should improve the alignment of the teacher with downstream objectives, leading to better performance of the distilled student. However, it may require additional computational resources for the adaptation step and may introduce additional biases or instabilities due to the learned reward model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of Distillation Error Inheritance
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of imperfections in the teacher's generative modeling and under-alignment of the pre-trained teacher with downstream preferences on the distilled student's performance. This will involve evaluating the student on a range of downstream tasks and comparing its performance against a teacher that is explicitly optimized for those tasks. Additionally, analyze the error transmission and alignment degradation during distillation, using techniques such as attribution methods or prototype-based representations to visualize and understand the flow of errors from the teacher to the student.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher-student pipeline with and without adaptation, as well as against a baseline that uses the original teacher without pre-training on downstream tasks (to study the impact of under-alignment).
COST: Estimated 1000 GPU-hours for a text-to-image generation task with a batch size of 32 and 1000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The analysis should provide valuable insights into the error inheritance problem and help identify the sources of degradation during distillation. However, it may require careful task selection and design to accurately capture the impact of under-alignment and error transmission.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: Develop a method for adversarial training of discrete generators, focusing on overcoming the challenges introduced by the non-differentiable sampling process. This will involve applying recent advancements in differentiable adversaries and loss functions, such as the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) or the Wasserstein discriminator, to discrete generator models.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the method on text-to-image synthesis and class-conditional image generation tasks, comparing against a baseline that uses the standard generator loss function and a method that uses the Gumbel-softmax relaxation with a straight-through estimator.
COST: Estimated 2500 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 128 and 5000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The method has the potential to improve the quality of generated samples by encouraging the generator to produce more realistic and diverse outputs. However, its effectiveness will depend on the choice of loss function and adversary architecture, and may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to optimize performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Discrete Generators (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal from Turn 5 to incorporate the differentiable token relaxation from the Gradient Flow Through the Teacher-Student Pipeline proposal, and apply it to the adversarial training method. This will allow the generator to produce soft, continuous outputs that can be compared to the real data by the discriminator, making the training process differentiable.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original adversarial training method, as well as against a version that uses the Gumbel-softmax relaxation with a straight-through estimator, but without the differentiable token relaxation.
COST: Estimated 2000 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 64 and 4000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The revised approach has the potential to improve the stability and efficiency of adversarial training for discrete generators, by allowing the use of differentiable losses and adversaries. However, it may still require careful tuning of hyperparameters to optimize performance, and may introduce additional biases or instabilities due to the relaxation of the discrete output.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Post-Distillation Refining with Learned Alignment
PROPOSAL: Develop a method for post-distillation refinement of one-step discrete generators, focusing on learning an alignment between the generator's outputs and the downstream objectives, such as aesthetic quality or prompt-following. This will involve learning a mapping from the generator's outputs to the downstream objectives, and using it to refine the generator's outputs through gradient-based optimization.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the method on text-to-image synthesis and class-conditional image generation tasks, comparing against a baseline that uses the original distilled generator and a method that uses pre-distillation refinement with a fixed alignment.
COST: Estimated 3000 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 128 and 6000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The method has the potential to improve the alignment of the generator's outputs with downstream objectives, leading to better performance and more interpretable results. However, its effectiveness will depend on the design of the learned alignment and the quality of the downstream objectives, and may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to optimize performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Analysis of Distillation Error Inheritance (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal from Turn 3 to focus on a more specific aspect of distillation error inheritance: the impact of teacher drift on downstream performance. This will involve analyzing the difference in performance between the distilled student and the original teacher on downstream tasks, and comparing it to the teacher's performance on the same tasks before and after distillation. Additionally, explore the use of a teacher update strategy, such as a meta-learning approach, to adapt the teacher to the downstream objectives and reduce the drift.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline that uses the original teacher without pre-training on downstream tasks, as well as against a version that uses a fixed teacher that is explicitly optimized for the downstream objectives.
COST: Estimated 1500 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 64 and 2000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The revised approach has the potential to provide valuable insights into the teacher drift problem and help identify the sources of performance degradation during distillation. However, it may require careful selection of downstream objectives and teacher architectures to optimize performance and reduce drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Pre-Training in One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of pre-training on the performance of one-step discrete generators, and explore whether pre-training can be used to improve the quality of distilled models. This will involve comparing the performance of one-step generators that are pre-trained on a large dataset before distillation to those that are trained from scratch, and analyzing the effectiveness of different pre-training objectives and architectures.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline that uses a generator that is trained from scratch, as well as against a version that uses a fixed pre-trained teacher that is explicitly optimized for the downstream objectives.
COST: Estimated 2500 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 128 and 5000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The investigation has the potential to provide valuable insights into the role of pre-training in one-step generators and help identify the best practices for pre-training and distillation. However, it may require careful selection of pre-training objectives, architectures, and downstream objectives to optimize performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Balancing Teacher and Student Complexity during Distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of teacher and student complexity on the quality of distilled models, and explore whether balancing the complexity of the teacher and student can improve the quality of distilled models. This will involve analyzing the effect of teacher and student architectures on the distilled model's performance, and exploring techniques such as regularization and weight sharing to balance their complexity.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline that uses a teacher and student with default architectures, as well as against versions that use different regularization techniques and weight sharing methods to balance complexity.
COST: Estimated 3000 GPU-hours for a text-to-image synthesis task with a batch size of 128 and 6000 iterations.
PREDICTION: The investigation has the potential to provide valuable insights into the trade-off between teacher and student complexity and help identify the best practices for architecting and distilling models. However, it may require careful selection of architectures, regularization techniques, and weight sharing methods to optimize performance.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Investigating Classifier-Free Guidance for Finite-Speed Kac Flows
PROPOSAL: We will re-design the guidance scheme used in diffusion models for finite-speed Kac flows by introducing a stochastic noise term that correlates with the conditional class distribution, while modifying the unconditional predictor to decorrelate its output from the class label. This ensures that the guidance signal remains informative but does not directly influence the flow's velocity.
CONTROLS: We will compare our re-designed guidance scheme against the standard classifier-free guidance for diffusion models and an unconditional version of the guidance scheme. Additionally, we will ablate the role of the stochastic noise term and the unconditional predictor modifications. 
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our re-designed guidance scheme will lead to comparable or better quality samples than standard classifier-free guidance for diffusion models, while maintaining the bounded-energy property of the Kac flow. If the stochastic noise term or unconditional predictor modifications are removed or altered, we expect a noticeable decrease in sample quality.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Few-Step Sampling for Finite-Speed Kac Flows
PROPOSAL: We will investigate using a multiscale sampling strategy and iteratively conditioning finetune Kac flows to achieve high-quality samples with few network evaluations. Specifically, we will: (1) start with a coarse initial guess obtained through a heuristic multi-step process; (2) gradually refine this guess by iteratively applying a specialized version of the Kac flow conditioned on the previous guess; and (3) use this iterative refinement to obtain the final sample.
CONTROLS: We will compare our few-step sampling strategy against standard reverse-time samplers for diffusion models, and ablate the role of each iteration and the conditioning steps. We will also measure the impact of varying the number of initial guess steps, the maximum number of iterations, and the specificity of the condition factors on sample quality and computational time.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our few-step sampling strategy will achieve higher-quality samples than diffusion-based samplers with a comparable computational budget, especially for highly Abby-Conventions conditional class distributions, while limiting the impact on computational time.

In addition to the multiscale sampling strategy and iteratively conditioning steps, we now include a stability analysis experiment where we: evaluate the impact of conditioning factors and step count on sample quality over an extended range of possible hyperparameters characterizing the conditional Kac flow; monitor the effective jump rate and speed of the underlying Poisson process for sub,jumps along the flow trajectory; and gage a radius of validity for the local convergence of the few-step conditioning steps, along the solution manifold using a series of radius sufficient conditions to measure its proximity to nonfailure of overall stability. Numerical evaluations will be conducted under uncertainty over a predefined domain of region samples of the domain distributions.

actions.texte:
ADD
TITLE:  Investigating Robustness of Time Series Foundation Models to Data Quality Issues
PROPOSAL: Train and evaluate the performance of three time series foundation models - TransFOXL (a sequence-to-sequence model), Transformers TCN (a temporal convolutional network), and TimeBert (a lightweight temporal attention mechanism) - on two datasets with varying levels of data quality ( synthetically corrupted M4 dataset and real-world electricity load forecasting dataset from Cmu Electricity dataset). We will assess model robustness by evaluating their ability to handle missing values, outliers, and irregular sampling.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline performance of the three models on clean datasets, (2) comparing model performance with and without data preprocessing techniques (e.g., imputation methods).
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect TransFOXL to be less robust to data quality issues due to its reliance on sequence-to-sequence architecture. Transformers TCN may perform moderately well due to its use of temporal convolution, while TimeBert should be robust due to its ability to adapt to varying sampling rates. This experiment may fail if the data corruption techniques used are too subtle, leading to minimal performance differences between the models.

Experiment-specific comments:

- The TransFOXL model is particularly well-suited for sequence-to-sequence tasks such as machine translation and text summarization, but it  relies heavily on well-structured input data, which can be a hindrance when dealing with time-series datasets marred by quality issues.
- TimeBert has shown impressive performance in handling irregularly sampled data which presents itself in various time series scenarios. 
- The choice of datasets for our study will allow for an in-depth analysis of the candidates's capability to abate data corruption.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Time Series Data Quality Assessment Using Large Language Models (LLMs)
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether LLMs can accurately assess the quality of time series data by designing a set of prompts that guide them to identify characteristics indicative of high or low-quality data. Specifically, we will use the LAION-5B model to evaluate a diverse set of time series datasets from the five domains listed (electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting, weather forecasting, handwriting recognition).
CONTROLS: (1) baseline performance of human annotators, (2) evaluating the performance of different LLM models (e.g., LAION-3B, CLIP-ViT-B-32) and prompt designs.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the LLMs to demonstrate a strong ability to identify high-quality time series data, especially in domains with well-defined patterns (e.g., weather forecasting). However, they may struggle with handwriting recognition data due to the visual nature of the data, which may not be well-represented in the LLM's training data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Prompt Design for Time Series Data Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Conduct an extensive evaluation of different prompt designs to assess their effectiveness in guiding LLMs to identify quality issues in time series data. Specifically, we will (1) compare the performance of various prompt designs (e.g., focused on missing values, outliers, or irregular sampling), (2) investigate the impact of prompt length and complexity, and (3) analyze the influence of instruction encoding techniques (e.g., instruction encoding with a dedicated instruction encoder and the instruction encoder as part of the model's transformer decoder).
CONTROLS: (1) using the same LLM and dataset as in proposal 1, (2) comparing the performance of a human-annotated baseline and a random labeling baseline.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect more complex prompts to be less effective due to the increased risk of ambiguity and misinterpretation. Instruction encoding techniques may lead to improved performance by enabling the LLM to better understand the prompt, but the effect is likely to be marginal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Attention Patterns for Time Series Data Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Investigate the attention patterns of LLMs when tasked with assessing the quality of time series data. By analyzing the attention weights assigned to different tokens and time steps, we can gain insights into how the LLMs process and reason about quality-related information. This study will focus on the transformer architectures of the LLMs and will evaluate the impact of attention heads, layer depth, and prompt design on the attention patterns.
CONTROLS: (1) comparing the attention patterns of different LLM models, (2) analyzing the attention patterns in the presence and absence of quality-related information in the prompt.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the attention patterns to reflect the quality-related information in the prompt, with a higher concentration of attention weights on tokens indicative of high-quality data. The effect of attention heads and layer depth is likely to be marginal, while prompt design may have a more significant influence on the attention patterns.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Prompt Design for Time Series Data Quality Assessment
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the prompt design evaluation to include a more nuanced analysis of prompt interpretability and comprehensibility. We will incorporate methods from natural language processing (NLP) and human-AI collaboration (HCI) to assess the ease of understanding and explainability of the prompts used in proposal 2. Additionally, we will incorporate a user study to gather feedback from human evaluators on the effectiveness and clarity of the prompts.
CONTROLS: (1) using the same LLM and dataset as in proposal 1, (2) incorporating multiple human evaluators from diverse backgrounds to gather feedback on the prompts.
COST: 2200 GPU-hours (additional computational resources for user study and NLP/HCI analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised prompt designs to demonstrate improved interpretability and comprehensibility, leading to better performance on the time series data quality assessment task. However, there may be a trade-off between prompt sophistication and human understanding, requiring careful balance to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Prompt Design for Time Series Data Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: As revised, the evaluation will assess not only the effectiveness of different prompt designs but also their interpretability and comprehensibility. We will use metrics from NLP and HCI, such as BERT-score and Human Evaluation Score (HES), to evaluate the quality of the prompts. To better understand how humans interact with prompts, we will carry out a user study with human evaluators.
CONTROLS: (1) using the same LLM and dataset as in proposal 1, (2) incorporating multiple human evaluators from diverse backgrounds to gather feedback on the prompts.
COST: 2200 GPU-hours (additional computational resources for user study and NLP/HCI analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised prompt designs to demonstrate improved interpretability and comprehensibility, leading to better performance on the time series data quality assessment task. However, there may be a trade-off between prompt sophistication and human understanding, requiring careful balance to achieve optimal results.

The analysis from this revised proposal will provide insights into the factors that influence human-AI collaboration in time series data quality assessment tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time Series Data Augmentation for Robust Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of data augmentation techniques on the robustness of LLMs in assessing time series data quality. We will apply various data augmentation methods (e.g., Fourier transform, Wavelet transform, and lengths adaptation) to a set of diverse time series datasets and evaluate how these changes impact the model's ability to identify high-quality data.
CONTROLS: (1) analyzing the impact of data augmentation on the LLM's performance on clean and noisy datasets, (2) comparing the robustness of LLMs trained with and without data augmentation.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect data augmentation to have a positive impact on the model's robustness, as it allows LLMs to learn more generalizable features. However, the effectiveness of data augmentation methods may depend on the type of time series data and the specific quality assessment task, requiring careful evaluation of different settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Time Series Quality Assessment Across Domains
PROPOSAL: Investigate the ability of LLMs to transfer knowledge from one time series domain to another when it comes to quality assessment. We will train a set of LLMs on multiple time series datasets from different domains (e.g., weather forecasting, traffic forecasting, and electricity load forecasting) and evaluate their performance on unseen domains.
CONTROLS: (1) analyzing the performance of LLMs trained on a single domain versus multiple domains, (2) comparing the performance of LLMs with and without fine-tuning on the target domain.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect LLMs trained on multiple domains to demonstrate better transferability and robustness to unseen domains, enabling them to make more accurate quality assessments. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may depend on the similarity between the source and target domains, requiring careful evaluation of different settings.

These experiments will build on the findings from previous proposals, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the relationships between LLMs, prompt design, and time series quality assessment.

COST: TBA based on the complexity of the theory-driven experiments
PREDICTION: This step will reveal potential research gaps and avenues for further investigation, allowing us to design a set of theory-driven experiments that can advance our understanding of time series quality assessment.

However, the effectiveness of data augmentation methods may depend on the type of time series data and the specific quality assessment task, requiring careful evaluation of different settings.

Investigate the ability of LLMs to transfer knowledge from one time series domain to another when it comes to quality assessment. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may depend on the similarity between the source and target domains, requiring careful evaluation of different settings.

Based on the insights gained from previous proposals, we will develop a comprehensive framework for time series quality assessment that integrates both data- and theory-driven approaches. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Domain Adaptation on Time Series Data Quality Estimation using Pretrained Language Models
PROPOSAL: We investigate the performance of using a range of pretrained language models (LLMs) -- specifically, distilBERT, RoBERTa, and T5 -- to estimate the quality of time series data from multiple domains (electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting, weather forecasting), with domain adaptation performed using a small task-specific dataset. This approach aims to leverage the LLM's ability to generalize across domains while still allowing for adaptation to domain-specific characteristics.
CONTROLS: Compare to: (1) standard fine-tuning of the LLM on each domain's specific data, (2) no adaptation (using the pre-trained model directly), and (3) a time series data quality estimation method that doesn't rely on LLMs (e.g., TimeInf).
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Given that LLMs are known to perform well on adapting to new domains, we expect the domain-adapted LLMs to outperform standard fine-tuning and itself without adaptation, but still potentially struggling with data quality estimation in complex domains like traffic forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Quality Criteria for Time Series Data via Human Evaluation
PROPOSAL: We conduct a human evaluation study where experts in relevant domains (e.g., energy, finance, transportation) are asked to assess the quality of time series data samples from multiple domains (electricity load forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, traffic forecasting) based on a set of pre-defined quality criteria (e.g., stationarity, periodicity, amplitude range). This will help us establish a benchmark for evaluating the performance of automated data quality estimation methods, including the use of LLMs.
CONTROLS: Use a subset of the same data samples for LLM-based data quality estimation and compare with human evaluations as a ground truth.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (for preparation and selection of data samples, and minor annotation effort)
PREDICTION: The human evaluation study should provide valuable insights into the types of quality criteria that are most important for time series data and highlight potential challenges for LLMs and other automated methods, such as capturing nuances of multiple quality criteria in complex domains.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Domain Adaptation on Time Series Data Quality Estimation using Pretrained Language Models
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal by introducing an active learning component to the domain adaptation process. This allows the model to learn from both unlabeled in-domain data and labeled out-of-domain data, improving its ability to generalize across domains. Specifically, we use a pool-based active learning strategy where the model chooses the most uncertain samples from a large pool of unlabeled data for labeling by human annotators.
CONTROLS: Compare to: (1) the original domain adaptation method without active learning, (2) random sampling of samples from the pool for active learning, and (3) a method that uses a fixed amount of labeled data without adaptively selecting samples.
COST: 120 GPU-hours (increased computational cost due to active learning and subsequent re-training)
PREDICTION: By actively selecting samples for human annotation, we expect the model to improve its performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain time series data quality estimation tasks, particularly in complex domains like traffic forecasting.

This includes assessing the model's ability to identify characteristics such as stationarity, periodicity, amplitude range, and noise level in the data.
CONTROLS: Use the same active learning strategy and domain adaptation method as before, and compare results across different quality criteria.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised model should demonstrate improved performance across multiple quality criteria, confirming the effectiveness of the domain adaptation method and active learning strategy. However, it may struggle with more nuanced quality criteria, such as identifying subtle patterns in noise.
