actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Establishing the necessity of strict equivariance in metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Theoretically investigate if strict equivariance is necessary for metanetworks by analyzing the implications of relaxing equivariance on the preservation of functional equivalence classes. Formulate a specific scenario in which a map relaxing strict equivariance still preserves functional identity.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed relaxation to existing metanetwork architectures enforcing strict equivariance and to uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines that rely on raw parameters.
COST: 10 GPU-hours, primarily used for theoretical derivations and MCMC sampling from the proposed relaxation.
PREDICTION: The proposed relaxation will preserve functional identity, but it may fail in cases where the relaxed symmetry does not align with the true symmetry group of the input architecture.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating relaxed equivariance through implicit neural representation editing
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a relaxed equivariance approach for implicit neural representation editing, specifically for refining the output weights of a given network architecture. Use a learnable, soft-enforcing mechanism to maintain functional identity under permutations, scaling, and sign changes of the weights.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed edited models to baseline models modified solely through random weight perturbations and to baseline metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance. Evaluate on the pre-images problem of retrieving the original network weights given the edited weights and the network architecture.
COST: 50 GPU-hours, used for evaluating editing performance on various scenarios, architectures, and evaluation metrics (e.g., pre-image recovery accuracy, edit stability).
PREDICTION: The proposed editing approach will demonstrate improved functionality preservation under permuted, scaled, or sign-changed weights, showing improved stability in pre-image recovery compared to baselines. However, it may require adjustments to the learnable soft enforcement to avoid overfitting or loss of expressivity.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Experiments on symmetry-consistent generalization prediction using real-world benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance and the proposed relaxation on a set of real-world benchmarks for predicting neural network generalization from weights. Specifically, use architectural characteristics (e.g., depth, width, activation functions) as inputs to the metanetworks and evaluate their performance on generalization prediction tasks (e.g., predicting validation loss, accuracy).
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed relaxation to metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, to uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines, and to state-of-the-art generalization prediction models. Evaluate on a diverse set of architectures and datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10, ImageNet).
COST: 100 GPU-hours, used for large-scale training and evaluation of metanetworks on various architectural characteristics and generalization prediction tasks.
PREDICTION: The proposed relaxation will show competitive performance on generalization prediction tasks, outperforming baselines where equivariance is not enforced and matching or slightly outperforming metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance in some cases.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Analyzing the representational power of relaxed equivariance in implicit neural representation classification
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of relaxed equivariance on the representational power of metanetworks in implicit neural representation classification tasks (e.g., predicting the architecture or activation functions of a given network). Evaluate the performance of metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, the proposed relaxation, and uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines on a range of classification tasks and datasets (e.g., classifying activation functions, predicting network widths).
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed relaxation to metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance and to uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines. Analyze the effects of the learnable soft enforcement on the representational power of the metanetworks.
COST: 30 GPU-hours, used for training and evaluating metanetworks on various classification tasks and datasets.
PREDICTION: The proposed relaxation will demonstrate improved representational power in implicit neural representation classification tasks, allowing metanetworks to better utilize the symmetries in the input weights and achieve competitive or superior performance compared to metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance. However, it may require careful tuning of the soft enforcement to avoid overfitting or loss of generalizability.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Improved representational power of relaxed equivariance in implicit neural representation classification
PROPOSAL: Extend the investigation of relaxed equivariance in implicit neural representation classification by exploring the benefits of using a hierarchically structured learnable soft enforcement, allowing the metanetwork to adapt to different levels of symmetry in the input weights. Specifically, consider using a layered soft enforcement architecture where the weights of the layers are subject to different levels of relaxation.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hierarchical soft enforcement metanetworks to the original relaxation, as well as to metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance and uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines. Analyze the effects of the hierarchical structure on the representational power of the metanetworks.
COST: No additional cost as this is a refinement of proposal 4.
PREDICTION: The hierarchical soft enforcement will demonstrate improved representational power in implicit neural representation classification tasks, allowing metanetworks to adapt to different levels of symmetry in the input weights and achieving superior performance compared to the original relaxation. However, it may require careful tuning of the hierarchical structure to avoid overfitting or loss of generalizability.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Empirical study of functionally equivalent neural network architectures
PROPOSAL: Investigate properties of functionally equivalent neural network architectures using the proposed relaxation of strict equivariance. Specifically, train a large collection of neural networks with different architectures but equal functionality, and analyze the effects of the relaxed equivariance on identifying functionally equivalent networks. Use a variety of architectures and evaluation metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1-score, precision) to quantify the benefits of the relaxed equivariance.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to baseline metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, as well as to uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines. Evaluate the robustness of the results to different network architectures and evaluation metrics.
COST: 200 GPU-hours, used for training and evaluating a large collection of neural networks with different architectures.
PREDICTION: The proposed relaxation will improve the identification of functionally equivalent neural network architectures, allowing metanetworks to better distinguish between networks that compute the same function despite differences in architecture. However, the quality of the metanetworks may degrade for very complex or irregular networks.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: On the learnability of equivariance and its relaxed counterparts
PROPOSAL: Theoretically investigate the learnability of equivariance and its relaxed counterparts in metanetworks, focusing on the effects of data distribution shifts, regularization, and optimization algorithms on the convergence of metanetworks to the target equivariance structure. Develop tools for analyzing the convergence rates of metanetworks under different learning conditions and derive conditions for when relaxation is beneficial.
CONTROLS: Compare the theoretical results to empirical observations and explore the implications for designing metanetworks and learning strategies that tackle real-world challenges.
COST: 20 GPU-hours, primarily used for theoretical derivations and numerical experiments.
PREDICTION: The results will provide insights into the conditions under which metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, and relaxed equivariance, converge to the desired function, and shed light on the role of data distribution shifts, regularization, and optimization algorithms in this process. However, applying these insights in practice may involve significant additional computation and expertise.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Robustness analysis of metanetworks under perturbations of input weights and architectures
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of metanetworks, including those enforcing strict equivariance and relaxed equivariance, to various perturbations of the input weights and architectures. Specifically, consider input weight noise, random perturbations of the architecture, and various regularization techniques. Analyze how the rejection rate of functionally equivalent networks changes under these perturbations and assess the trade-offs between robustness and expressivity.
CONTROLS: Compare the robustness of well-regularized metanetworks to those with limited regularization, and examine the impact of different types of regularization on robustness and predictive performance.
COST: 150 GPU-hours, used for perturbation analysis and robustness experiments.
PREDICTION: The results will provide insights into the robustness-regularization trade-offs in metanetworks and reveal the benefits of well-regularized architectures under weight and architecture perturbations.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Improved relaxed equivariance for neural network generalization prediction with implicit neural representations
PROPOSAL: Refine the proposed relaxation of strict equivariance by incorporating knowledge-distillation and transfer learning techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of generalization prediction. Specifically, incorporate domain-specific features and knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network to augment the representation learning of the metanetwork.
CONTROLS: Compare the refined relaxation to existing metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, well-regularized metanetworks, and uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines.
COST: 100 GPU-hours, used for training and evaluation of the refined metanetworks on various generalization prediction tasks.
PREDICTION: The refined relaxation with knowledge-distillation and transfer learning will show improved accuracy and robustness in neural network generalization prediction, making metanetworks more effective at identifying functionally equivalent networks and extracting implicit neural representations.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: Neural network comparison using relaxed equivariance and differentiable architecture search
PROPOSAL: Combine the proposed relaxation of strict equivariance with differentiable architecture search to develop a principled method for comparing and evaluating the architecture of neural networks. Specifically, use the relaxed equivariance to evaluate the compatibility of different architecture components and the overall architecture, and apply differentiable architecture search to find the optimal architecture.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to metanetworks enforcing strict equivariance, well-regularized metanetworks, and uninformed parameter-augmentation baselines.
COST: 300 GPU-hours, used for training and evaluation of the combined method on various neural network architecture comparison tasks.
PREDICTION: The combined method will demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency in comparing and evaluating neural network architectures, thanks to the principled relaxation of strict equivariance and the differentiable architecture search approach.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Necessity of Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Design a case study analyzing the role of strict equivariance in a synthetic metanetwork dataset where the input networks have known architectures and weights. This study will vary the model architectures processed by the metanetwork, and evaluate whether strict equivariance is necessary for accurate generalization prediction from weights.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that relies solely on raw parameters, and ablate the strict equivariance constraint by removing it from the metanetwork's architecture.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that strict equivariance is not necessary for generalization prediction from weights in all cases, and that the removal of this constraint may lead to improved model expressivity. However, certain architectures or weight configurations may still require strict equivariance to maintain accurate predictions. Failure to see a significant improvement may indicate that our current understanding of metanetworks does not fully capture the complexity of the parameter spaces they operate on.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Exactness of Weight-Level Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Theoretically investigate the conditions under which weight-level equivariance is exact in metanetworks operating on multi-layer perceptrons. Identify symmetry groups of the architecture that guarantee (or preclude) exact equivariance, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the lifted representation that preserve (or undermine) the ensured symmetry.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing case studies and analyses on analogous weight-level equivariance.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that weight-level equivariance is exactly preserved for a broad class of multi-layer perceptrons, specifically those featuring symmetries from the permutational wreath product. However, other architectures such as multihead attention networks or mixture-of-experts layers may exhibit non-exact equivariance due to internal permutation symmetries. If we fail to establish exact equivariance in the expected cases, this may have significant implications for the design of practically-efficient and invariant metanetworks.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exactness of Weight-Level Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: REVISED - Theoretically investigate the relationship between the symmetries of multi-layer perceptron architectures and the lifted representation in metanetworks. Develop a rigorous proof that for specific symmetry groups of the MLP architecture, the lifted representation exhibits exact equivariance. Identify classes of MLPs where weight-level equivariance holds, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the model architecture for exact equivariance to occur.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing case studies and analyses on analogous weight-level equivariance.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (-5 due to revision)
PREDICTION: We expect to find exact weight-level equivariance for a more general class of MLPs than previously known, specifically those featuring symmetries from the permutational wreath product. However, we may still find cases where non-exact equivariance prevails due to internal permutation symmetries.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the performance of strict permutation-equivariant metanetworks to non-equivariant metanetworks on the task of neural network generalization prediction from weights. Specifically, we train metanetworks on the weights of pre-trained neural networks using a dataset of neural network architectures, and evaluate their ability to predict test set performance on unseen networks. We also analyze the effect of equivariance on model expressivity and training dynamics.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Non-equivariant metanetwork (no symmetry enforcement)
- Baseline 2: Strict permutation-equivariant metanetwork (previous state-of-the-art)
- Ablation study: Remove symmetry enforcement to see if strict equivariance is necessary for good performance
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect strict equivariance to provide some benefit over non-equivariance, but also expect it to impose a penalty on expressivity, leading to a trade-off between these two factors. If the baseline 2 is significantly better than baseline 1, this would suggest that strict equivariance is a useful inductive bias for metanetworks. If, however, baseline 1 outperforms baseline 2, it could indicate that strict equivariance is not necessary for good performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Characterizing the Symmetry Groups of Convolutional Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework for characterizing the symmetry groups of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), specifically with respect to permutation and scaling symmetries. This framework can be used to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a metanetwork to be equivariant or invariant to these symmetries, and provide insights into the structure of the function class implemented by CNNs.
CONTROLS: 
- Review of existing results on symmetry groups of CNNs
- Connections to metanetwork equivariance
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to be able to derive general conditions for a metanetwork to be equivariant or invariant to permutation and scaling symmetries, which can be used to develop new equivariant metanetwork architectures that are tailored to the properties of CNNs.

Note: This proposal is theoretical in nature, and does not require extensive computational resources.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: REVISED: Expand the scope of the experiment to include multiple metanetwork architectures and focus on the specific case of implicit neural representation classification. This includes revising the experiment to use a dataset of implicit neural representations and replace the neural network generalization prediction task with implicit neural representation classification. The rest of the proposal remains the same.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Non-equivariant metanetwork (no symmetry enforcement)
- Baseline 2: Strict permutation-equivariant metanetwork (previous state-of-the-art)
- Ablation study: Remove symmetry enforcement to see if strict equivariance is necessary for good performance
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the results to complement those obtained from the original experiment, providing insights into the performance of metanetworks on a different task and potentially shedding light on their capability to capture symmetries in implicit neural representations.

ACTION: REVISE 2 title to better reflect the focus on CNNs
TITLE: Characterizing the Symmetry Groups of Convolutional Networks
PROPOSAL: REVISED: Focus on deriving a novel theoretical result: a necessary and sufficient condition for a metanetwork to be invariant to scaling symmetries of convolutional neural networks. This will help develop new metanetwork architectures that can preserve the function class implemented by CNNs under scaling transformations.
CONTROLS: 
- Review of existing results on symmetry groups of CNNs
- Connections to metanetwork invariance
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the derived condition to provide a useful tool for designing metanetworks that are invariant to scaling symmetries of CNNs, allowing for more accurate preservation of the function class implemented by these networks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Soft Equivariant Metanetworks for Modeling Symmetries in Implicit Neural Representations
PROPOSAL: Design and train a metanetwork with a soft equivariance constraint, which relaxes the strict permutation equivariance of weights. This metanetwork will be trained on a task such as implicit neural representation classification and evaluated on its performance compared to a strict equivariance baselines. We will also investigate the effect of varying the temperature of the softmax function used in the soft equivariance constraint on the metanetwork's performance.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Strict permutation-equivariant metanetwork
- Baseline 2: Non-equivariant metanetwork (no symmetry enforcement)
- Ablation study: Vary the temperature of the softmax function to see its impact on the metanetwork's performance
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the soft equivariant metanetwork to perform better than the non-equivariant baseline while still providing more flexibility than the strict equivariance baseline. The ablation study on the temperature of the softmax function will provide insights into the optimal level of soft equivariance for good performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: REVISED: Include a new control group that trains a metanetwork with a learning objective that preserves the functional equivalence classes of the parameters, but does not enforce strict equivariance. This can be done by adding a term to the metanetwork's loss function that encourages the model to output the same prediction for different parameterizations of the same function.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Non-equivariant metanetwork (no symmetry enforcement)
- Baseline 2: Strict permutation-equivariant metanetwork (previous state-of-the-art)
- Baseline 3: Metanetwork that preserves functional equivalence classes (new control group)
- Ablation study: Remove the functional equivalence preserving term to see its impact on the metanetwork's performance
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the metanetwork that preserves functional equivalence classes to outperform the non-equivariant baseline, and potentially rival the performance of the strict equivariance baseline. If the functional equivalence preserving term has a significant impact on the metanetwork's performance, this could suggest that it is a useful inductive bias for metanetworks.

ACTION: REVISE 3 title to better reflect the focus on soft equivariance
TITLE: Soft Equivariant Metanetworks for Modeling Symmetries in Implicit Neural Representations
PROPOSAL: REVISED: Include a theoretical analysis of the relationship between soft equivariance and strict equivariance. Specifically, we will derive a bound on the difference between the performance of a soft equivariant metanetwork and a strict equivariance metanetwork, providing insights into the trade-offs between these two inductive biases.
CONTROLS: 
- Review of existing results on soft equivariance and strict equivariance
- Theoretical analysis of the relationship between these two inductive biases
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the bound to provide a useful tool for understanding the trade-offs between soft equivariance and strict equivariance, and potentially shed light on the optimal level of equivariance for different tasks and metanetwork architectures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Metanetworks to Architectural Perturbations
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of metanetworks to architectural perturbations, such as adding or removing layers, or modifying the activation functions. This can be done by training metanetworks on a dataset of perturbed architectures and evaluating their performance on a test set of unperturbed architectures. We also expect to compare the robustness of strict equivariant, soft equivariant, and non-equivariant metanetworks.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Non-equivariant metanetwork (no symmetry enforcement)
- Baseline 2: Strict permutation-equivariant metanetwork (previous state-of-the-art)
- Baseline 3: Soft equivariant metanetwork (previous state-of-the-art)
- Ablation study: Vary the level of perturbation to see its impact on the metanetwork's performance
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the strict equivariant metanetwork to be more robust to architectural perturbations than the soft equivariant and non-equivariant metanetworks, due to its ability to preserve the symmetries of the architecture. However, this may come at the cost of increased brittleness to overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metanetwork-based Bayesian Neural Networks for Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a metanetwork-based Bayesian neural network (BNN) that can estimate the uncertainty of a neural network's predictions. This can be done by building a metanetwork that takes the weights and architecture of a neural network as input, and outputs a probabilistic distribution over the network's predictions. We will then compare the performance of our metanetwork-based BNN to traditional BNNs.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Traditional BNN (existing state-of-the-art)
- Ablation study: Remove the metanetwork component to see its impact on the BNN's performance
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the metanetwork-based BNN to provide a more accurate estimate of uncertainty, due to its ability to leverage the symmetries of the neural network's architecture. However, this may come at the cost of increased computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Survey of Metanetworks for Deep Learning
PROPOSAL: Write a comprehensive survey paper that reviews the recent advances in metanetworks for deep learning, including their applications, architectures, and theoretical foundations. We will cover the topics of strict equivariance, soft equivariance, and metanetwork-based Bayesian neural networks, as well as their connections to other areas of machine learning and computer science.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 0 (text-only research)
PREDICTION: We expect the survey paper to provide a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of deep learning, and to help shape the future direction of research in metanetworks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A  Baseline Study on Global-View MLLMs' Fine-Grained VQA Performance
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the state-of-the-art global-view MLLMs (CLIP and ALBEF) on several fine-grained VQA benchmarks (Functional-Object-Navigation, Visual-Reasoning-Sets, Textbook-VQA) and their corresponding global-view downsampling settings in pixel resolutions 224, 256, 288, and compare their performance metrics (accuracy, Fleiss' Kappa) to those obtained by applying various shortcut knowledge-agnostic heuristics such as ICM (Inter-Classbird and Multitask) and averging fixed pre-defined areas associated with common objects dimensions: e.g. mouths 10cm in diameter.
CONTROLS: FLAX model with a ResNet-50-based encoder, training P and Q transformers without learning and with the much-simplified repeated cross-modal setting and averaged pre-activation mixed operations.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (2 months on 1- 8A60S GPUs)
PREDICTION: Returns low values of accuracy and high discrepancy when compared with particular areas of expertise among imbalanced objects capacity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration of Efficient Hierarchical Search Methods for Visual Cropping
PROPOSAL: Implement and compare three more efficient hierarchical search methods for visual cropping on the fine-grained VQA task: (1) Hierarchical Centroid-based Search (HCS), where the model starts by cropping a quarter of the image and refines the crop to a smaller region based on a centroid computed from the question-relevant regions; (2) Quad-Tree-based Search (QTS), where the image is recursively divided into quadrants and only the quadrant with the maximum predicted relevance is explored; and (3) Prim's Algorithm-based Search (PAS), where the model efficiently discovers the minimum spanning tree connecting the question-relevant regions. The proposed approaches will be evaluated on benchmark datasets like Visual Genome, Imagenet VQA and Taskonomy.
CONTROLS: Visualization-based pooling with ResNet-101 encoder for different visualsearch sizes, Territory estimator function: Endeavor N, Effective probabilistic-meny translator
COST: 1200 GPU-hours (4 months on 4- 8A60S GPUs)
PREDICTION: The proposed methods will show improved efficiency (2-5x) compared to exhaustive search methods, while yielding competitive performance (±2%) compared to global-local-view MLLMs, on fine-grained VQA tasks.

TITLE: Hybrid Visual Cropping Approach for Fine-Grained VQA
PROPOSAL: Develop a hybrid visual cropping approach that combines the benefits of efficient hierarchical search methods (e.g., EPA) with the power of contrastive learning frameworks (e.g., CEL) for visual cropping. PREDICTION: Expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks while reducing computational cost by 20%-30% compared to existing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Deployment and Evaluation of Visual Cropping
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of the hybrid visual cropping approach on real-world high-resolution images from various domains, including autonomous driving, remote sensing imagery, OCR in real-world images, diagram and table understanding, and video surveillance monitoring. This involves collecting and pre-processing real-world datasets from these domains, and then using the hybrid visual cropping approach to evaluate its performance on these datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hybrid visual cropping approach to other state-of-the-art visual cropping methods on these real-world datasets, and evaluate its performance using metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and AUC-ROC.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours (10 months on 5- 8A60S GPUs)
PREDICTION: Expected to demonstrate the effectiveness of the hybrid visual cropping approach on real-world high-resolution images and provide insights into its strengths and limitations in different domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimization of Visual Cropping for Edge Devices
PROPOSAL: Optimize the hybrid visual cropping approach for deployment on edge devices, such as smartphones, smart glasses, or autonomous vehicles, which have limited computational resources and memory. This will involve quantizing the model, pruning the weights, and using knowledge distillation to reduce the computational requirements while maintaining the performance of the original model.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the optimized model on various edge devices, and compare its performance to other state-of-the-art visual cropping models optimized for edge devices.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (4 months on 2- 8A60S GPUs)
PREDICTION: Expected to demonstrate that the optimized model can achieve competitive performance on edge devices while reducing the computational requirements by 50% or more, making it suitable for real-time deployment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Visual Cropping and Fine-Grained VQA
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework that integrates the hybrid visual cropping approach with the fine-grained VQA model to address the challenge of visual cropping and VQA in a single pass. This will involve modifying the fine-grained VQA model to incorporate the region proposals generated by the hybrid visual cropping approach and to adaptively learn the relevant regions for each question.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the unified framework on a variety of fine-grained VQA benchmarks and compare its performance to other state-of-the-art visual cropping and VQA models.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (3 months on 1- 8A60S GPU)
PREDICTION: Expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks while reducing the computational requirements by 20%-30% compared to existing methods, making it a highly competitive solution for real-world applications.

propositions.prediction: Expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks while reducing the computational requirements by 20%-30% compared to existing methods, making it a highly competitive solution for real-world applications.
propositions.texte: Develop a unified framework that integrates the hybrid visual cropping approach with the fine-grained VQA model to address the challenge of visual cropping and VQA in a single pass. This will involve modifying the fine-grained VQA model to incorporate the region proposals generated by the hybrid visual cropping approach and to adaptively learn the relevant regions for each question.
propositions.titre: A Unified Framework for Visual Cropping and Fine-Grained VQA

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Efficient Visual Attention Meets Localized Visual Search
PROPOSAL: Compare the inference cost and performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks of Prompty, which focuses the attention of the MLLM on the region of the image guided by the question, versus a local-view MLLM (such as MLP-Mixer or MSETTER) on both real-world images from the VG-BIRDS dataset and high-resolution images from the HR-VQA dataset. To reduce the search space, Prompty will be allowed to attend only to pre-determined patches from a sparse pyramid representation of the image.
CONTROLS: Global-view MLLM (Bart-Large), global-local-view MLLM (T5-Large+MSETTER), and, as baseline, a relevance-based visual cropping method, ViCrop, which will be forced to only take a single region as input to mimic the localized search.
COST: 18k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Prompty should significantly outperform the global-view MLLM on fine-grained tasks while keeping inference cost roughly comparable to global-local-view MLLMs.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Region Guidance through Symbolic Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Implement a symbolic reasoning module on top of the MLLM to generate a symbolic graph representation of the image which can guide the local-attention of Prompty. The symbolic representation will capture object relationships and recognize abstract concepts that co-occur with the query. To further aid the localization process, condition the symbolic graph generation on the query using a graph-structured approach such as SCAN or GraphCodeBERT.
CONTROLS: Same as before: global-view MLLM (Bart-Large), global-local-view MLLM (T5-Large+MSETTER), Prompty without the symbolic reasoning module, and ViCrop as a baseline.
COST: 20k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Adding the symbolic reasoning module should improve the performance of Prompty on VQA tasks by enabling the model to better understand question-specific visual relationships, and its efficiency will remain comparable to that of the global-local-view MLLM.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Efficient Visual Attention Meets Localized Visual Search (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Improve upon the previous version by allowing Prompty to selectively focus on relevant regions rather than being restricted to pre-determined patches from a sparse pyramid representation. Achieve this by introducing a multi-branch architecture, where the input to Prompty is split into a coarse-scale feature map and a fine-scale feature map, and the model outputs two sets of attention weights – one for each scale. Train this multi-branch architecture with a joint loss function that optimizes both region localization and VQA task performance.
CONTROLS: Same as before: global-view MLLM (Bart-Large), global-local-view MLLM (T5-Large+MSETTER), Prompty without the multi-branch architecture, and ViCrop as a baseline.
COST: 25k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new architecture should significantly boost the performance of Prompty on fine-grained tasks, enabling it to adaptively select the regions of interest from the input image.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Robust Localized Visual Search
PROPOSAL: Evaluate Prompty and its variants on high-resolution images from datasets related to autonomous driving, remote sensing imagery, and OCR in real-world images – specifically, the IDD dataset, the UAVDT dataset, and the ICDAR 2015 dataset, respectively. Fine-tune Prompty using transfer learning, with the goal of adapting its localized visual search capabilities to these novel domains with varying visual characteristics and object sizes. Assess its robustness by swapping between these datasets and fine-tuning it with few-shot learning.
CONTROLS: Fine-tune Prompty separately on each of the three datasets and a baselines that don't use transfer learning (random initialization and train from scratch), as well as with the previously introduced Region Guidance through Symbolic Reasoning module.
COST: 22k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Transfer learning and few-shot learning can enable Prompty to generalize well to novel domains with varying object sizes and visual characteristics, consistently outperforming models that are not fine-tuned for these tasks.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Scalable Pyramid Pooling for Real-World Images
PROPOSAL: Implement a scalable pyramid pooling mechanism as a pre-processing step for input images. This mechanism aims to efficiently capture multi-scale information from the input images while adapting to different image resolutions. Apply it to high-resolution images from the experimental domains, reducing the computational cost of localized visual search while maintaining its accuracy. Compare Prompty's performance on images pre-processed via scalable pyramid pooling (SPP-Prompty) against images processed without it (Raw-Prompty) and global-local-view MLLMs.
CONTROLS: Same as before, plus a baseline that does not use pyramid pooling, and results will be compared on HR-VQA and IDD datasets.
COST: 18k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Adding SPP as a pre-processing step should significantly reduce the computational cost of localized visual search (approximately 5x less than Raw-Prompty) while providing a modest improvement in performance, particularly for images with diverse object sizes and scales.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Visual Adversarial Training for Robust Localized Visual Search
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of Prompty under various visual adversarial attacks, which aim to mislead the model by manipulating the input images. Design a visual adversarial training (VAT) procedure to equip Prompty with robustness against such attacks, enabling it to maintain high accuracy on noisy or perturbed inputs. Evaluate its performance on both clean and adversarially attacked images, examining whether VAT enhances its ability to localize relevant regions in real-world images.
CONTROLS: Baseline models include Prompty without VAT, synthetic variants of it with randomly added perturbations, SPP-Prompty and Vanilla-Prompty, with corresponding VAT variants for robustness enhancement. 
COST: 25k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The addition of VAT to Prompty will make it more robust against visual adversarial attacks and localized visual search will remain accurate even on perturbed images, although there may be a small performance drop on clean data due to added training complexity.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Scalable Pyramid Pooling for Real-World Images (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Enhance the scalability of the pyramid pooling mechanism by adding a learned hierarchical representation of the image into the scalable pyramid pooling network. This can be achieved by incorporating a pre-trained hierarchical feature extractor, such as ConvNeXt or Swin Transformer, directly into the pyramid pooling module. This revised version, Hierarchical SPP, combines the computation and representational capabilities of heterogeneous architectures, allowing for more flexible and efficient multi-scale processing of high-resolution images.
CONTROLS: All baselines from previous experiments remain, in addition to a new, more complex baseline that replaces the SPP module with a pre-trained hierarchical encoder.
COST: 20k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised pyramid pooling mechanism will demonstrate better scalability and improved efficiency for processing high-resolution images without compromising generalization, further enhancing the localized visual search capabilities of Prompty variants.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Edge-Centric Visual Attention for Fine-Grained Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Extend the localized visual search capabilities of Prompty to support edge-centric visual attention, enabling it to better focus on fine-grained details and nowadays exemplify high level feature representations from edge information that accompany the appearance information of target objects. Incorporate an Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Fusion module to reweight multi-scale feature maps according to their edge-based saliency to the query.
CONTROLS: This experiment compares Prompty variants with the Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Fusion module (EAMSF-Prompty) against its counterparts without it, and Object Detection models to establish an evaluation baseline.
COST: 22k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: EAMSF-Prompty will outperform its counterparts and significantly improve local object detection accuracy in a fine-grained visual question answering, and edge-salient pixels transferred from images can dramatically boost Prompty's edge-aware understanding.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Robust Localized Visual Search (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a domain-invariant learning (DIL) approach into the transfer learning process to make Prompty more robust to shifts between domains and datasets. Specifically, utilize DIL to learn domain-invariant representations for input images and query questions, which can be more transferable across datasets with varying visual characteristics and object sizes. This revised transfer learning pipeline can enable Prompty to generalize better to novel tasks and domains with wider variability in images and query questions.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Robust Evaluation on Large-Scale Vision-and-Language Benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Scale up localized visual search experiments to large-scale vision-and-language benchmarks such as the Visual Genome dataset and the VQA Large-scale dataset. Assess the robustness and generalization capabilities of Prompty and its variants across diverse scenarios, including those with sparse or occluded objects, diverse visual backgrounds, and varying levels of image resolution. Evaluate their performance in terms of accuracy, inference time, and computational cost.
CONTROLS: This experiment adds large-scale benchmark datasets to previous experiments, expanding the set of evaluation metrics and tasks to measure localized visual search capabilities on ultra-large datasets.
COST: 40k GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results on these large-scale benchmarks will demonstrate that enhanced localized visual search capabilities persist even on very large datasets, while efficiently gaining performance while reducing costs for inference.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Efficient Hierarchical Visual Cropping for Global-View MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate a hierarchical visual cropping approach that partitions the image into smaller regions through a series of splits based on the MLLM's confidence scores in predicting the answer to the fine-grained VQA task. This is inspired by the idea of self-paced learning, where the model learns to focus on the most informative regions of the image through an iterative process.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of downsampling the image to the base resolution of the MLLM's vision encoder, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of the hierarchical structure.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see an improvement in accuracy compared to the downsampling baseline, but may struggle to match the performance of more complex and computationally expensive methods. This approach may also require fine-tuning the model for each new dataset.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Simple yet Effective Contextual Visual Cropping for Global-Local-View MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Introduce a contextual visual cropping approach that utilizes the output of the MLLM's encoder to determine the most informative regions of the image. This approach involves transforming the output feature maps of the encoder into a probability density function, which can be used to sample regions of interest from the original image.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of a simple random cropping strategy and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of different probability density functions.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see a moderate improvement in accuracy compared to the random cropping baseline, and potentially outperforming the hierarchical visual cropping approach from proposal 1 in certain scenarios. However, it may struggle to scale up to larger image sizes due to computational complexity.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Simple yet Effective Contextual Visual Cropping for Global-Local-View MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Modify the contextual visual cropping approach in proposal 2 to include a spatial attention mechanism that focuses on the regions of the image that are most relevant to the question being asked. This is achieved by applying a self-attention layer to the output feature maps of the encoder.
CONTROLS: Compare against an ablation study to evaluate the impact of the spatial attention mechanism, and a baseline of a simple random cropping strategy.
COST: 70 GPU-hours (increased due to the additional self-attention layer)
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in accuracy compared to the random cropping baseline, and potentially outperforming the hierarchical visual cropping approach from proposal 1. However, it may also be more computationally expensive due to the added self-attention layer.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Learning for Transferable Visual Cropping
PROPOSAL: Develop a semi-supervised learning approach that allows the MLLM to learn a visual cropping strategy on a large unlabeled dataset of images, and then fine-tune this approach on a smaller labeled dataset of fine-grained VQA examples. This approach enables the model to learn transferable visual cropping knowledge that can be applied to multiple tasks and datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare against a supervised learning baseline, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of the semi-supervised learning approach.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in transferability and adaptability across different datasets and tasks, and potentially outperforming other visual cropping approaches in certain scenarios. However, it may also require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Visual Cropping with Question-Guided Pooling
PROPOSAL: Introduce a weakly-supervised visual cropping approach that utilizes a question-guided pooling mechanism to identify the most relevant regions of the image for a given question. This approach is based on a simple yet effective pooling strategy that selects the most discriminative features from the output of the MLLM's encoder.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of a random cropping strategy, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of different pooling mechanisms.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see a moderate improvement in accuracy compared to the random cropping baseline, and potentially outperforming the contextual visual cropping approach in proposal 2 in certain scenarios. However, it may also require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Visual Cropping with Question-Guided Pooling
PROPOSAL: Modify the question-guided pooling mechanism in proposal 4 to incorporate attention weights learned from a contrastive learning framework. This allows the model to selectively focus on the most informative regions of the image while preserving the spatial relationships between features.
CONTROLS: Compare against an ablation study to evaluate the impact of the contrastive learning framework, and a baseline of a simple random cropping strategy.
COST: 180 GPU-hours (increased due to the additional contrastive learning framework)
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in accuracy compared to the random cropping baseline, and potentially outperforming the contextual visual cropping approach in proposal 2 and the weakly-supervised visual cropping approach in the revised proposal 4. However, it may also be more computationally expensive due to the added contrastive learning framework.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Hybrid Visual Cropping with Hierarchical and Contextual Strategies
PROPOSAL: Develop a hybrid visual cropping approach that combines the strengths of hierarchical visual cropping (proposal 1) and contextual visual cropping (proposal 2). The model first partitions the image into smaller regions using hierarchical visual cropping, and then selectively focuses on the most informative regions using contextual visual cropping.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of a single hierarchical or contextual visual cropping approach, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of different combinations of hierarchical and contextual strategies.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline approaches, and potentially outperforming the transferable visual cropping approach in proposal 3. However, it may also be more computationally expensive due to the increased complexity of the hybrid approach.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Large-Scale Transfer Learning for Visual Cropping with Class-Attention
PROPOSAL: Utilize a large-scale transfer learning approach that fine-tunes a pre-trained visual cropping model on a wide range of image classification tasks, while incorporating class-attention to focus on the most relevant regions of the image for each task.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of a smaller-scale transfer learning approach, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of class-attention.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in transferability and adaptability across different tasks and datasets, potentially outperforming other visual cropping approaches, including the hybrid visual cropping approach in proposal 5. However, it may also be more computationally expensive due to the large-scale transfer learning.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Active Learning for Visual Cropping with Human-in-the-Loop
PROPOSAL: Develop an active learning approach for visual cropping that involves a human-in-the-loop to select the most informative regions of the image for further labeling. This approach enables the model to collect high-quality data more efficiently and improve its accuracy over time.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of passive learning, and an ablation study to evaluate the impact of different active learning strategies.
COST: 400 GPU-hours (note: human annotation time is not included in this estimate)
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline approaches, and potentially outperforming the large-scale transfer learning approach in proposal 6. However, it may also be more time-consuming and labor-intensive due to the human-in-the-loop process.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Radio Frequency-based Neural Implicit Reconstruction for Near-range Objects
PROPOSAL: We will train a neural implicit representation on mmWave radar data from near-range objects (e.g., objects in a box), leveraging a modified version of the SIREN (Sinusoidal Embedding for Real-valued Energy-based Networks) architecture, which is capable of learning a function that maps mmWave inputs to a 3D grid representing the object's geometry. We will use the 'Millimeter Resolution Radar' (M3R) dataset for training and validation, which contains mmWave radar images of near-range objects. We will also fine-tune different architectures of SIREN and NEU-SDF (Neural occupancy field UnStructured Field with an implicit surface Defining Function), taking into account previously identified causes of the model's instability when approximating propagation characteristics of RF signals for individual objects.
CONTROLS: Ablation studies on SIREN variants without a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) refinement network, functional configuration, and model-specific sample representations will be included to determine their effectiveness. A comparison with known beamforming-based mmWave reconstruction algorithms and neural-based non-line-of-sight through-wall sensing methods will serve as a baseline to quantify performance improvements. Baseline evaluations will also be performed without any implicit surface defining in a feature-transform technique (FT) registration methods.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected reconstruction accuracy for 3D object shapes is anticipated to reach up to 0.8 mm. However, due to the RF specificity and neural approximations at near range, prediction is challenging with flavour for considerably strict combinations of position and human constraints setups in both training and deployment scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Validated Optimizers for Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will develop and analyze different optimizers and training strategies for the neural implicit representation to improve its performance and stability on RF data, particularly for near-range objects. This includes using Adam with Waight scheme, using quantification and normalized range conversion techniques that scale input signals to improve low amplitude gradient loss in each signal layer. Furthermore, we will investigate the use of transfer learning with pre-trained weights and data augmentation techniques to make the model more robust against variations in RF signals. This will be validated on the 'M3R' dataset and at real-world embeddings with state-of-art resolution on various simulated near-range objects occlusion models.
CONTROLS: We will compare the optimizers' performance with the baseline trained using the Adam optimizer and evaluate the performance of the pre-trained model with fine-tuning on different real-world benchmarks to determine whether it improves the accuracy and generalizability of the neural RF reconstruction. The effect of different training strategies (number of epochs, batch size, learning rate) will also be analyzed. 
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected accuracy gain due to optimized training is anticipated to reach about 15-20% improvement.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Real-World Validated Optimizers for Neural RF Reconstruction (Revision)
PROPOSAL: We will extend the experiment in Turn 2, to also investigate the effect of regularization techniques on the performance and stability of the neural implicit representation. This includes implementing dropout, L1 and L2 regularization, early stopping, and weight decay to mitigate overfitting and promote generalization. We will also evaluate the performance of the model with a gradient penalty to encourage the model to produce smooth reconstructions.
CONTROLS: The same controls as before, with the additional evaluation of the regularization techniques' impact on the model's performance. We will also compare the performance of the model with and without the gradient penalty.
PREDICTION: Expected regularizing impact is to help increasing prediction metrics by a further 8-12% over a 10% of already beta ignorant regression logarithm mean processors.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Real-World Validated Optimizers for Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will also evaluate the impact of incorporating priors and constraints into the neural implicit representation to improve its performance and robustness on RF data, particularly for near-range objects. This includes exploring the use of prior knowledge about the object's shape, pose, and symmetry, as well as incorporating spatial and range-related constraints to guide the reconstruction. Additionally, we will investigate the effect of using different constraint types, such as midpoint constraints or splitting constraints, to improve the model's performance.
CONTROLS: The effect of incorporating priors and constraints will be compared against the baseline model without them. We will also evaluate the impact of incorporating multiple priors and constraints simultaneously.
COST: 550 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected increase in accuracy and robustness of the neural RF reconstruction is anticipated to reach 10-15% due to the informed constraint evaluation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-Aware Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a physics-aware neural RF reconstruction method that incorporates physical models of RF propagation and interaction with the environment. This includes using ray tracing algorithms to simulate the RF signal propagation and incorporating physical models of object reflection, absorption, and scatter. The goal is to improve the accuracy and robustness of the neural RF reconstruction by leveraging the physical properties of RF signals. This will be validated on the 'M3R' dataset and real-world benchmarks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the physics-aware model against the baseline neural implicit representation model and evaluate the impact of using different physical models and simulation resolutions.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in reconstruction accuracy is anticipated to reach 20-25% due to the incorporation of physical models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of multi-modal data fusion to improve the accuracy and robustness of neural RF reconstruction. This includes combining RF data with other modalities such as camera images, lidar points, or other sensors that can provide complementary information about the object's shape and appearance. We will evaluate the use of different fusion techniques, such as early fusion, late fusion, and hybrid fusion, to determine the most effective approach.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the multi-modal model against the baseline neural implicit representation model and evaluate the impact of using different fusion techniques and sensor modalities.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in reconstruction accuracy is anticipated to reach 15-20% due to the incorporation of complementary information from other sensors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a semi-supervised neural RF reconstruction method that can learn from both labeled and unlabeled data. This includes using techniques such as self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, and pseudo-labeling to leverage the large amounts of unlabeled data available for RF sensing. The goal is to improve the accuracy and robustness of the neural RF reconstruction by reducing the need for labeled data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the semi-supervised model against the baseline neural implicit representation model and evaluate the impact of using different semi-supervised learning techniques and amounts of labeled data.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in reconstruction accuracy is anticipated to reach 18-22% due to the ability to leverage unlabeled data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Neural RF Reconstruction for Streaming Data
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate an online neural RF reconstruction method that can process streaming data in real-time. This includes using techniques such as online learning, incremental learning, and streaming data aggregation to handle the continuously arriving data. The goal is to enable real-time neural RF reconstruction for applications such as surveillance, robotics, and smart cities.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the online model against the baseline neural implicit representation model and evaluate the impact of using different online learning techniques and data streaming rates.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in real-time reconstruction accuracy is anticipated to reach 10-15% due to the ability to process streaming data in real-time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exemplar-Based Neural RF Reconstruction for Partially Occluded Objects
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate an exemplar-based neural RF reconstruction method that can reconstruct objects from partial and occluded observations. This includes using techniques such as Exemplar-based neural networks and partial matching to use known patterns from the training data to fill in missing information and correct for partial occlusions. The goal is to improve the accuracy and robustness of the neural RF reconstruction in real-world scenarios where objects may be partially occluded.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the exemplar-based model against the baseline neural implicit representation model and evaluate the impact of using different exemplar-based learning techniques and occlusion levels.
COST: 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in occluded object reconstruction accuracy is anticipated to reach 20-25% due to the ability to utilize patterns from known objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Deployment and Evaluation of Neural RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will deploy and evaluate the neural RF reconstruction methods on real-world hardware and in real-world scenarios, such as the millimeter resolution radar system (M3R) used for object tracking and level sensing, and other real-world industrial or healthcare applications. This includes evaluating the performance of the models in terms of speed, accuracy, and robustness in real-world environments, as well as exploring applications and use cases for neural RF reconstruction.
CONTROLS: We will compare the real-world performance of the neural RF reconstruction methods against existing state-of-the-art methods and evaluate the impact of different hardware and software configurations on the performance of the models.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours (estimated hardware testing time)
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in real-world deployment and evaluation is anticipated to lead to adoption in industrial or healthcare applications due to the accuracy and robustness of the neural RF reconstruction methods.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 3D Reconstruction from Noisy mmWave Radar Data using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: This experiment utilizes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) that incorporates the forward model of mmWave radar imaging to reduce the effect of noise in the input data. Specifically, we formulate the radar signal as a function of the object's surface geometry, radar antenna array parameters, and environmental factors. The PINN learns a mapping from the input radar data to the estimated 3D surface geometry of the object. We evaluate the proposed method on real-world mmWave radar data collected from various objects in boxes, with and without occlusions.
CONTROLS: We compare our method to a baseline that uses a standard neural network architecture without the physical constraints. We also perform an ablation study to evaluate the importance of incorporating the forward model in the network. In addition, we compare our method to the state-of-the-art method proposed by [1].
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in reconstructing the 3D surface geometry of objects from noisy mmWave radar data. However, the method may fail to accurately capture small features or details in the object's geometry due to the high level of noise in the input data.

[1] Zhang et al., "Millimeter-Wave Radar Imaging of 3D Object Shape with Deep Learning", IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 2022.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Specular Reflections on mmWave Radar Imaging
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to study the effect of specular reflections on mmWave radar imaging and 3D reconstruction. We simulate various scenes with different levels of specular reflections and estimate the resulting radar signal using a physics-based model. We then compare the accuracy of different 3D reconstruction algorithms (e.g., point cloud-based, mesh-based) in handling specular reflections. Specifically, we investigate whether incorporating the simulated radar signal into the reconstruction pipeline can mitigate the effects of specular reflections.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed method to a baseline that does not account for specular reflections. We also evaluate the impact of different simulation parameters (e.g., reflection coefficients, radar frequencies) on the reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This study is expected to reveal the limitations of current 3D reconstruction algorithms in handling specular reflections and provide insights into the development of more robust and accurate methods for mmWave radar imaging.

Note: This proposal is relevant to the experimental domain of mmWave radar imaging and through-occlusion imaging of objects in boxes.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Specular Reflections on mmWave Radar Imaging
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to study the effect of specular reflections on mmWave radar imaging and 3D reconstruction. We collect real-world mmWave radar data from objects with varying levels of specular reflections and use it to train a 3D reconstruction model. We then evaluate the performance of the model in reconstructing the object's geometry in different scenarios. Specifically, we investigate whether the model can accurately capture the object's surface features, such as edges and corners, which are commonly affected by specular reflections.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed method to a baseline that assumes only diffuse reflections. We also evaluate the impact of different data augmentation techniques (e.g., rotation, scaling) on the model's ability to handle specular reflections.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This study is expected to demonstrate the robustness of the 3D reconstruction model in handling specular reflections and provide insights into the development of more robust and accurate methods for mmWave radar imaging.

Note: This revised proposal is now relevant to the experimental domain of millimeter-wave radar imaging and through-occlusion imaging of objects in boxes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compression of Radar Signals using Autoencoders for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to compress mmWave radar signals into a lower-dimensional representation using a neural network-based autoencoder. We evaluate the compressed signal representation in a 3D reconstruction task, with a focus on reducing the noise and increasing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We compare the performance of the proposed method to traditional signal processing techniques, such as filtering and downsampling.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed method to a baseline that uses a standard neural network architecture without compression. We also evaluate the impact of different autoencoder architectures (e.g., convolutional, recurrent) on the compression quality and reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 125 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method is expected to significantly reduce the noise in mmWave radar signals and improve the accuracy of 3D reconstruction. However, the compression quality may degenerate if the signal is already sparse or has a high SNR.

Note: This proposal is relevant to the experimental domain of millimeter-wave radar imaging and RF-based 3D object shape reconstruction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Multi-Resolution Representations for mmWave Radar Imaging
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to investigate the use of multi-resolution representations for mmWave radar imaging and 3D reconstruction. We use a feature pyramid network (FPN) architecture to extract features at multiple resolutions and evaluate its performance in reconstructing the 3D geometry of objects. We compare the proposed method to a baseline that uses a single-resolution representation.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed method to a baseline that uses a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. We also evaluate the impact of different pyramid scales and activation functions on the reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method is expected to improve the accuracy of 3D reconstruction by capturing both local and global features in the mmWave radar signals. However, the computational cost may increase due to the use of multiple resolutions.

Note: This proposal is relevant to the experimental domains of millimeter-wave radar imaging and RF-based 3D object shape reconstruction.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Compression of Radar Signals using Autoencoders for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to further improve the compression quality of mmWave radar signals using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a non-Gaussian prior. We evaluate the compressed signal representation in a 3D reconstruction task and compare its performance to that of the original autoencoder and a baseline that uses traditional signal processing techniques.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed method to a baseline that uses a standard neural network architecture without compression. We also evaluate the impact of different VAE architectures (e.g., convolutional, recurrent) and prior distributions on the compression quality and reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method is expected to further improve the compression quality and reduce the noise in mmWave radar signals, leading to more accurate 3D reconstruction. However, the computational cost may increase due to the use of a VAE with a non-Gaussian prior.

Note: This revised proposal aims to improve the reconstruction accuracy by leveraging the strengths of Variational Autoencoders in modeling complex prior distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Validation of mmWave Radar-Based 3D Reconstruction in Occluded Scenarios
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to evaluate the performance of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction methods in real-world, through-occlusion scenarios. We collect real-world mmWave radar data from various objects hidden behind occlusions and compare the performance of different 3D reconstruction methods (e.g., the ones proposed in this paper) to a baseline that uses only point cloud data.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed methods to a baseline that uses a standard point cloud processing pipeline. We also evaluate the impact of different occlusion types (e.g., blocking, masking) and radar frequencies on the reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 180 GPU-hours (not including data collection and preprocessing)
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to demonstrate the potential of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction in real-world, through-occlusion scenarios and provide insights into the challenges and limitations of this approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards Explainable mmWave Radar-Based 3D Reconstruction: Visualizing and Understanding the Reconstruction Process
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to develop techniques for visualizing and understanding the reconstruction process of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction methods. We propose a novel visualization framework that allows users to inspect the reconstruction process and identify potential errors or areas of improvement. We also investigate the use of attention mechanisms and other explainability techniques to improve the transparency and interpretability of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction models.
CONTROLS: We compare the effectiveness of different visualization techniques and explainability methods on improving the interpretability and transparency of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction models.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method is expected to improve the trust and reliability of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction models by providing users with a deeper understanding of the reconstruction process and enabling the identification of potential errors or areas of improvement.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Multi-Resolution Representations for mmWave Radar Imaging
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to improve the multi-resolution representation approach proposed in the original experiment. We introduce a novel scheme for selecting the optimal pyramid scale and activation function for each resolution level, based on the characteristics of the radar signal and the object being reconstructed. We also investigate the use of a hierarchical attention mechanism to focus on the most informative features at each resolution level.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the revised method to the original multi-resolution representation approach and evaluate the impact of different pyramid scale and activation function selection schemes on the reconstruction accuracy.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised method is expected to further improve the accuracy and efficiency of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction, particularly for objects with complex geometries or multiple occlusions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalability and Real-Time Capabilities of mmWave Radar-Based 3D Reconstruction Methods
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to evaluate the scalability and real-time capabilities of the mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction methods proposed in this paper. We assess the computational complexity and latency of each method, and explore strategies for reducing computational overhead, such as parallelization, server-side processing, and transfer learning.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed methods to state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction algorithms, and evaluate the impact of different hardware platforms and software frameworks on the reconstruction speed and accuracy.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (not including hardware and software setup)
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to provide insights into the scalability and real-time capabilities of mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction methods, and facilitate the development of efficient and real-time capable systems for mmWave radar-based 3D reconstruction.
