actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Sampling of Distinct Semantic Outputs for Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Implement a diversity-oriented sampling strategy that uses an iterative prompting mechanism to discover semantically diverse outputs from a given set of generative models (e.g., Llama or Flan-T5). Each prompt will be designed to encourage the model to generate a new, semantically distinct output. To improve efficiency, we will employ a graph-based clustering method to group similar outputs together and allocate more samples to clusters with the highest diversity.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard sampling methods (e.g., random sampling, nucleus sampling) and our own implementation without clustering.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly improve the diversity of the sampled outputs, making it easier to estimate semantic entropy and reducing the number of samples required to achieve a stable estimate. It could, however, fail if the graph-based clustering method fails to capture meaningful clusters, leading to inefficient allocation of samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Prompt Engineering for Epistemic Uncertainty Analysis
PROPOSAL: Develop a new prompting framework to iteratively query the model via a sequence of carefully crafted prompts that target specific aspects of its knowledge base. By observing the model's response to each prompt, we can gain insight into the areas where it feels uncertain or lacks knowledge. This framework will be validated on the question answering task, where a prompt sequence might include "What is the Hubble constant?", "How has it changed over time?", and "Can you explain the method used to measure it?". To quantify epistemic uncertainty, we will compute the mutual information between the prompt sequence and the model's output.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing methods that rely on iterative prompting (e.g., our previous proposal 1) and evaluate the effectiveness of different prompt engineering strategies.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our prompting framework should be able to identify knowledge gaps in the model and provide a lower bound on epistemic uncertainty. However, it could fail if the prompts are not carefully designed to target the relevant aspects of the model's knowledge base, leading to an incomplete picture of uncertainty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Masked Diffusion Models for Improved Uncertainty Quantification
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of masked diffusion models (MDMs) for uncertainty estimation in question answering tasks. We will fine-tune pre-trained MDMs on a question answering dataset and compare their performance to state-of-the-art autoregressive models (ARMs) in terms of predicting aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. To evaluate the MDM's ability to capture semantic uncertainty, we will use our proposed sampling method (proposal 1) to generate diverse outputs from the MDM and compute the semantic entropy.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art ARMs (e.g., Llama or Flan-T5) and evaluate the impact of different MDM architectures and hyperparameters on uncertainty estimation.
COST: 8,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: MDMs may offer an improvement over ARMs in terms of uncertainty estimation due to their ability to model complex dependencies in the input data. However, they may also suffer from higher computational costs and potentially overfit the training data, leading to poor generalization performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Refining Leveraging Prompt Engineering for Epistemic Uncertainty Analysis
PROPOSAL: Refine the prompting framework developed in proposal 2 by incorporating an additional "abstain" prompt, which queries the model to indicate when it is unsure or lacks knowledge about a particular topic. The model's response to this prompt will be used to compute an upper bound on epistemic uncertainty, providing a more comprehensive picture of uncertainty. To further validate the framework, we will also investigate the impact of different types of prompts (e.g., open-ended questions, multiple-choice questions) on epistemic uncertainty estimation.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original prompting framework without the "abstain" prompt and evaluate the effectiveness of different prompt types.
COST: Additional 1,000 GPU-hours (on top of the original 5,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The revised prompting framework should be able to provide a more accurate estimate of epistemic uncertainty, especially when the model is unsure or lacks knowledge about a particular topic. However, it could fail if the "abstain" prompt is not carefully designed to elicit a response from the model, leading to an incomplete or inaccurate picture of uncertainty.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Masked Diffusion Models for Improved Uncertainty Quantification
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of an extension to the masked diffusion model architecture that incorporates an auxiliary "confidence" model, trained to predict the confidence of the MDM's output on each task. This confidence model will be used in conjunction with the MDM to provide a more accurate estimate of epistemic uncertainty. Specifically, we will use the predictive uncertainty from the confidence model as an additional regularization term in the MDM's training objective.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original MDM architecture and evaluate the impact of different confidence model architectures on uncertainty estimation.
COST: Additional 3,000 GPU-hours (on top of the original 8,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The extended MDM architecture should be able to provide a more accurate estimate of epistemic uncertainty by incorporating the confidence model's predictive uncertainty. However, it could fail if the confidence model is not well-calibrated or fails to capture the underlying uncertainty in the data, leading to poor performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Uncertainty Estimation Methods on a Common Benchmark
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified benchmark for evaluating uncertainty estimation methods in question answering tasks, including proposals 1-3. The benchmark will consist of a set of carefully curated questions, along with their corresponding answers and uncertainty labels. We will use this benchmark to compare the performance of different uncertainty estimation methods on estimating aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing uncertainty estimation methods (e.g., temperature scaling, nucleus sampling) and evaluate the effectiveness of each method on the benchmark.
COST: 2,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The unified benchmark should provide a more comprehensive understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of different uncertainty estimation methods, enabling better comparison and selection of methods for real-world applications. However, it could fail if the benchmark is not well-designed or fails to capture the underlying performance of the methods being evaluated.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Evaluating Uncertainty Estimation Methods on a Common Benchmark
PROPOSAL: In addition to comparing the performance of different uncertainty estimation methods, we will also investigate the relationship between the estimation of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty and the model's performance on downstream tasks, such as question answering. Specifically, we will use the benchmark to evaluate the effect of different uncertainty estimation methods on the model's accuracy, F1-score, and other evaluation metrics.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original evaluation metrics used for the benchmark.
COST: No additional compute required (already included in the original 2,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The analysis should provide insights into the trade-offs between different uncertainty estimation methods and their impact on the model's performance. However, it could fail if the downstream tasks are not well-aligned with the uncertainty estimation tasks, leading to inconclusive results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Using Uncertainty Estimates to Improve Model Robustness
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of uncertainty estimates to improve the robustness of the model to adversarial attacks and out-of-distribution (OOD) examples. Specifically, we will use the uncertainty estimates to detect when the model is uncertain or has low confidence in its predictions, and use this information to adapt the model's behavior to avoid misclassifying OOD examples or producing inconsistent outputs under adversarial attacks.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art methods for model robustness, and evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of benchmarks and attack scenarios.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The approach should be able to improve the model's robustness to OOD examples and adversarial attacks, but may fail if the uncertainty estimates are not accurately calibrated or if the adaptation mechanism is not well-designed.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Using Uncertainty Estimates to Improve Model Robustness
PROPOSAL: We will extend the approach in proposal 5 to not only adapt the model's behavior to avoid misclassifying OOD examples or producing inconsistent outputs under adversarial attacks, but also use the uncertainty estimates to detect and correct for potential biases in the training data. Specifically, we will use the uncertainty estimates to identify regions of the input space where the model is least confident and adjust the training data accordingly to reduce potential biases.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original approach in proposal 5 and evaluate the impact of the bias correction mechanism on model robustness.
COST: Additional 2,000 GPU-hours (on top of the original 5,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The approach should be able to further improve the model's robustness and reduce potential biases in the training data, but may fail if the bias correction mechanism is not well-designed or if the uncertainty estimates are not accurately calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Model Selection for Real-World Applications
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of uncertainty estimates to inform model selection for real-world applications. Specifically, we will use the uncertainty estimates to compare the performance of different models on a given task and select the model that best matches the user's requirements and risk tolerance. To facilitate this process, we will develop a model selection framework that takes into account both the model's accuracy and its uncertainty estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing model selection methods that do not consider uncertainty estimates and evaluate the impact of uncertainty-aware model selection on real-world applications.
COST: 4,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The framework should be able to improve the accuracy and reliability of model selection for real-world applications, but may fail if the uncertainty estimates are not accurately calibrated or if the model selection framework is not well-designed.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Source of Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 2D Diffusion-Based 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will compare the accuracy of reconstructed volumes obtained by processing individual 2D slices independently via a pre-trained 2D diffusion model against a version that synchronizes the stochastic noise components across slices, similar to the remedy used in video restoration. This sync will be achieved by either sparingly interpolating shared noise between slices or by utilizing a shared noise vector for all slices at each diffusion step.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: standard slice-wise processing, Baseline 2: the sync remedy used in video restoration, Ablation 1: no synchronization across the x and y dimensions (only z).
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe improved inter-slice consistency but are uncertain whether synchronization fully addresses the root cause. We also anticipate temporal noise component synchronization to still degrade temporal fine details and potentially produce vignetting artifacts if not carefully calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Regularization for Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the idea of robustifying neural networks against adversarial examples, we propose an adversarial training technique to promote inter-slice consistency. Instead of using a traditional reconstruction loss, we train an auxiliary network that tries to contrast the results of slice-wise and synchronized processing. This auxiliary network applies pressure on the diffusion model to find reconstructions that are both accurate and consistent across slices, without strictly requiring the synchronized processing to be perfect.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: traditional reconstruction loss, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: no adversarial training.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By promoting consistency through an optimization process, we expect this approach to improve inter-slice consistency without the need for synchronized noise or additional hyperparameters. However, we also anticipate that this method might degrade the overall quality of the reconstructions due to the added complexity of the auxiliary network.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Adversarial Regularization for Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We modify the previous approach by incorporating an entropic regularization term between the output distributions of the sequential slices. This regularization term pushes the output of one slice to be close to the input of the subsequent slice, providing a consistent flow of information between the slices.
CONTROLS: Remains the same: Baseline 1: traditional reconstruction loss, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: no adversarial training.
COST: 22 GPU-hours (due to the minor modification, the overall cost increases slightly)
PREDICTION: By directly promoting a consistent flow of information, we expect this revised approach to further improve inter-slice consistency without introducing additional sensitivity to noise or model retraining costs.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Adversarial Regularization for Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We modify the previous approach by incorporating an entropic regularization term between the output distributions of the sequential slices. This regularization term pushes the output of one slice to be close to the input of the subsequent slice, providing a consistent flow of information between the slices.
CONTROLS: Remains the same: Baseline 1: traditional reconstruction loss, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: no adversarial training, Ablation 1: without labelling variables.
COST: 22 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By directly promoting a consistent flow of information, we expect this revised approach to further improve inter-slice consistency without introducing additional sensitivity to noise or model retraining costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Inter-Slice Consistency through Augmented Reverse Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: To eliminate the need for additional regularization or noise synchronization, we explore augmenting the reverse diffusion process itself. We introduce a learned residual function that maps the current noisy state at each time step to the previous state's output after denoising. By effectively "remembering" the previous state's output, we motivate the diffusion model to produce more consistent reconstructions between slices without requiring explicit synchronization or regularization.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: standard reverse diffusion process, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: no residual function, Baseline 4: notable modifications to the noise scheduling.
COST: 35 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By augmenting the reverse diffusion process, we expect to see improved inter-slice consistency without requiring additional optimization or hyperparameter tuning. However, the performance might be sensitive to the complexity and capacity of the residual function, which could result in overfitting or degradation of fine details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Inter-Slice Consistency in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical framework to understand the fundamental limits of inter-slice consistency in diffusion models. By analyzing the information-theoretic properties of the diffusion process, we derive bounds on the achievable consistency between consecutive slices. Furthermore, we investigate the role of noise synchrony and residual functions in enhancing consistency and provide recommendations for their effective design.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 5 GPU-hours (theoretical analysis requires minimal computational resources)
PREDICTION: Through this theoretical analysis, we expect to gain a deeper understanding of the mechanical reasons behind inter-slice inconsistency in diffusion models and derive insights for designing more consistent reconstruction pipelines. However, the applicability of these theoretical results to specific reconstruction tasks might be limited by the simplifying assumptions made during the analysis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Inter-Slice Consistency on Sparse-View CT Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We conduct experiments on a sparse-view CT reconstruction task to evaluate the inter-slice consistency of the methods proposed in this study. We use publicly available datasets and implementation models that specialize in CT reconstruction. We measure consistency using metrics such as mean absolute difference (MAD) and PSNR of adjacent slices.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: standard 3D reconstruction using a pre-trained 2D diffusion model, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: the inter-slice consistency through an augmented reverse diffusion process, Baseline 4: evaluated using the aforementioned metrics in a brain MRI isotropic super-resolution task.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe that our approaches lead to improved inter-slice consistency and superior reconstruction quality on sparse-view CT data. However, the differences between the competitors might be subtle, and it will require a careful evaluation and visual inspection of the results to determine the clear winner.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Transferability of Inter-Slice Consistency to Brain MRI Isotropic Super-Resolution
PROPOSAL: We conduct experiments to evaluate the transferability of the inter-slice consistency methods proposed in this study to brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We use a brain MRI dataset and train a pre-trained 2D diffusion model on the sparse-view CT task and apply it to brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We then apply our inter-slice consistency approaches to the MRI task and compare the results to the baselines.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: standard brain MRI isotropic super-resolution using a pre-trained 2D diffusion model, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: the inter-slice consistency through an augmented reverse diffusion process, Baseline 4: the inter-slice consistency via entropic regularization.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe that our inter-slice consistency approaches can be transferred to brain MRI isotropic super-resolution and improves the consistency and quality of the reconstructions. However, the effectiveness of the transferability might depend on the domain similarity between sparse-view CT and brain MRI isotropic super-resolution tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study on the Contributions of Individual Components
PROPOSAL: We conduct an ablation study to understand the individual contributions of the different components used in our proposed methods for inter-slice consistency. We remove each component one by one and evaluate the effect on the inter-slice consistency and overall reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: standard 3D reconstruction using a pre-trained 2D diffusion model, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes with all our proposed methods, Baseline 3: removing the entropic regularization, Baseline 4: removing the residual function, Baseline 5: removing the synchronization remedy, Baseline 6: removing the adversarial regularization.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (ablation study requires less computational resources compared to thorough evaluation)
PREDICTION: We expect to gain a better understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each component and identify which components are most crucial for achieving inter-slice consistency.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Inter-Slice Consistency through Augmented Reverse Diffusion Process
PROPOSAL: We refine our previously proposed augmented reverse diffusion process by incorporating a learned fusion mechanism to combine the information from adjacent slices in a more sophisticated way. PROPOSAL 1: Investigating the Source of Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 2D Diffusion-Based 3D Reconstruction
We will compare the accuracy of reconstructed volumes obtained by processing individual 2D slices independently via a pre-trained 2D diffusion model against a version that synchronizes the stochastic noise components across slices, similar to the remedy used in video restoration. This sync will be achieved by either sparingly interpolating shared noise between slices or by utilizing a shared noise vector for all slices at each diffusion step.
Controls: Baseline 1: standard slice-wise processing, Baseline 2: the sync remedy used in video restoration, Ablation 1: no synchronization across the x and y dimensions (only z).
Estimated cost: 10 GPU-hours
Prediction: We expect to observe improved inter-slice consistency but are uncertain whether synchronization fully addresses the root cause. We also anticipate temporal noise component synchronization to still degrade temporal fine details and potentially produce vignetting artifacts if not carefully calibrated.

PROPOSAL 2: Adversarial Regularization for Inter-Slice Consistency
We modify the previous approach by incorporating an entropic regularization term between the output distributions of the sequential slices. This regularization term pushes the output of one slice to be close to the input of the subsequent slice, providing a consistent flow of information between the slices.
Controls: Remains the same: Baseline 1: traditional reconstruction loss, Baseline 2: reconstructed volumes using the sync remedy, Baseline 3: no adversarial training, Ablation 1: without labelling variables.

PROPOSAL 3: Inter-Slice Consistency through Augmented Reverse Diffusion Process
We refine our previously proposed augmented reverse diffusion process by incorporating a learned fusion mechanism to combine the information from adjacent slices in a more sophisticated way. This fusion mechanism uses a conditional normalizing flow to progressively refine the output of the diffusion process, allowing for improved interslice consistency while preserving fine details.

PROPOSAL 4: A Theoretical Analysis of Inter-Slice Consistency in Diffusion Models
We provide a theoretical framework to understand the fundamental limits of inter-slice consistency in diffusion models. By analyzing the information-theoretic properties of the diffusion process, we derive bounds on the achievable consistency between consecutive slices. Furthermore, we investigate the role of noise synchrony and residual functions in enhancing consistency and provide recommendations for their effective design.

We conduct experiments on a sparse-view CT reconstruction task to evaluate the inter-slice consistency of the methods proposed in this study. We use publicly available datasets and implementation models that specialize in CT reconstruction. We measure consistency using metrics such as mean absolute difference (MAD) and PSNR of adjacent slices.

PROPOSAL 6: Investigating the Transferability of Inter-Slice Consistency to Brain MRI Isotropic Super-Resolution
We conduct experiments to evaluate the transferability of the inter-slice consistency methods proposed in this study to brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We use a brain MRI dataset and train a pre-trained 2D diffusion model on the sparse-view CT task and apply it to brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We then apply our inter-slice consistency approaches to the MRI task and compare the results to the baselines.

PROPOSAL 7: Ablation Study on the Contributions of Individual Components
We conduct an ablation study to understand the individual contributions of the different components used in our proposed methods for inter-slice consistency. We remove each component one by one and evaluate the effect on the inter-slice consistency and overall reconstruction quality.

Estimated cost: 25 GPU-hours (ablation study requires less computational resources compared to thorough evaluation)
Prediction: We expect to gain a better understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each component and identify which components are most crucial for achieving inter-slice consistency.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Slice-Wise Stochasticity in 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of independent slice-wise sampling on inter-slice consistency in 3D medical reconstruction using 2D diffusion priors by implementing a controlled baseline study consisting of 3D volumes reconstructed from 2D slices using different diffusion models (e.g., DALL-E, U-Net, SIREN) and analyzing the resulting volumes with metrics such as mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index (SSIM) between adjacent slices.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction techniques (e.g., ViT-DS, 3D U-Net, stack of 2D U-Nets) and augmentation techniques like slice-wise transform norms and Madzi et. al. Techniques.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This baseline study will reveal a significant degradation in inter-slice consistency caused by the independent slice-wise sampling process, with a potential for further improvement by optimizing the diffusion models and loss functions, and exploring noise regularization techniques such as injecting aligned noise patterns across adjacent slices.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Diffusion-Based Noise Synchronization
PROPOSAL: Modify the diffusion algorithm to introduce aligned noise patterns across adjacent slices by learning a noise representation using a small neural network (e.g., ResNet) and superimposing it on each slice before the forward diffusion pass, thus propagating coherent noise patterns through the volume. Evaluate the impact on inter-slice consistency using the metrics from proposal 1, and on volumetric reconstruction quality using metrics such as dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance.
CONTROLS: Compare against the baseline study (proposal 1) and against diffusion-based noise regularization techniques like the noise injection across frames to alleviate temporal flickering in video restoration.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve inter-slice consistency, yielding better volumetric reconstruction quality, but may introduce additional computational overhead and potentially squander fine diagnostic details.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Reverse Diffusion Coil
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel reverse diffusion coil mechanism that learns aligned noise patterns across adjacent slices during the reverse diffusion process, rather than just injecting them. The coil will consist of a small neural network that takes as input the current slice and its neighbors and predicts the aligned noise pattern. Evaluate the impact on inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality, as well as the computational overhead and potential for fine detail preservation.
CONTROLS: Compare against the noise synchronization (proposal 2), the baseline study (proposal 1), and other coherence-enhancing diffusion-based methods like coherence-based noise injection.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach aims to combine the benefits of noise regulation and reverse diffusion, potentially yielding better results than proposal 2, but may be computationally expensive and sensitive to noise level and network architecture design.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Reverse Diffusion Coil with Adaptive Noise Injection
PROPOSAL: Enhance the reverse diffusion coil mechanism (proposal 3) by adaptively adjusting the amount of injected noise based on the confidence of the predicted aligned noise pattern. Introduce an additional neural network that evaluates the confidence of the coil's prediction and scales the injected noise accordingly, allowing the coil to focus on areas of uncertainty and reduce noise in areas with higher confidence predictions. Evaluate the impact on inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original reverse diffusion coil (proposal 3), the noise synchronization (proposal 2), the baseline study (proposal 1), and other techniques that incorporate adaptive noise control.
COST: 220 GPU-hours (due to additional neural network complexity)
PREDICTION: This revised coil should improve the balance between coherence enhancement and fine detail preservation, while maintaining or reducing computational overhead compared to proposal 3.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Joint 2D/3D Prior Learning
PROPOSAL: Modify the training procedure of the 2D diffusion model to incorporate 3D volumetric reconstructions as an additional input, allowing the model to learn a joint 2D-3D prior that captures both the slice-wise relationships and the volumetric structure. Evaluate the resulting 2D model on 3D volumetric reconstructions and compare against the original 2D model and proposed coherence-enhancing techniques (proposals 2 and 3).
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline 3D reconstruction methods, state-of-the-art 3D-2D fusion techniques, and the proposed coherence-enhancing diffusion-based methods.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach may improve inter-slice consistency and overall reconstruction quality, but may require careful tuning of the joint 2D-3D prior learning objective and potentially increase training time and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Slice-Wise Attention-Based Reverse Diffusion
PROPOSAL: Introduce a slice-wise attention mechanism within the reverse diffusion coil (proposal 3), allowing the coil to selectively focus on specific slices when learning aligned noise patterns. This would enable the coil to adapt to varying levels of noise and coherence across the volume, improving inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original reverse diffusion coil (proposal 3), the noise synchronization (proposal 2), the baseline study (proposal 1), and other attention-based diffusion-based methods.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve coherence enhancement and fine detail preservation, particularly in areas with high variability in noise levels and anatomical structure. However, it may require careful tuning of attention mechanisms and risk overemphasizing certain slices at the expense of others.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Apply an unsupervised domain adaptation technique to the 2D diffusion model, allowing it to learn a consistent representation across different 3D volumes and improving its ability to generalize to new, unseen data. This would enable the model to better capture the underlying structure of the 3D anatomy, leading to improved inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Compare against the previous proposals, as well as baseline domain adaptation methods and state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction techniques.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the model's ability to generalize across different volumes and domain shifts, but may require careful selection of domain adaptation techniques and hyperparameters. It may also increase the risk of overfitting to specific domains or anomalies.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Multi-Scale Reverse Diffusion Coil
PROPOSAL: Modify the reverse diffusion coil (proposal 3) to operate on multiple scales, allowing the coil to capture meaningful patterns and structures at different resolutions. This would improve the coil's ability to learn aligned noise patterns and enhance inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original reverse diffusion coil (proposal 3), the noise synchronization (proposal 2), the baseline study (proposal 1), and other multi-scale diffusion-based methods.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should capture more detailed structures and patterns within the volume, improving the accuracy of the reconstruction, but may introduce additional computational overhead and complexity. It may also require careful tuning of the multi-scale architecture and coil mechanics.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Nested Lightweight Coils for Efficient Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Introduce a nested structure to the multi-scale reverse diffusion coil (proposal 7), where small, lightweight coils are used to predict aligned noise patterns at each scale, rather than a single large coil. This would significantly reduce the computational overhead and memory requirements, making the method more practical for large-scale 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original multi-scale reverse diffusion coil (proposal 7), other nested coil architectures, and baseline reconstruction methods.
COST: 180 GPU-hours (reduced from 350 due to nested coil architecture)
PREDICTION: This approach should efficiently capture the patterns and structures within the volume while reducing the computational burden, but may compromise some level of accuracy and complexity.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Slice-Wise Stochasticity in 3D Reconstruction with Nested Coils
PROPOSAL: Combine the nested lightweight coils (proposal 8) with the diffusion-based noise synchronization (proposal 2) and joint 2D/3D prior learning (proposal 4) to create a comprehensive framework for improving inter-slice consistency and volumetric reconstruction quality in 3D medical imaging. Evaluate the impact of the nested coils on the overall reconstruction performance and compare against state-of-the-art reconstruction methods.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original 3 proposals (2, 4, and 8), baseline reconstruction methods, and state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction techniques in sparse-view and limited-angle CT reconstruction and brain MRI isotropic super-resolution.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comprehensive framework should improve the reconstruction quality and inter-slice consistency, but may require careful tuning of the nested coil architecture and other hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 3D Medical Reconstruction with Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the inter-slice consistency of 3D medical reconstructions obtained by applying a pre-trained 2D diffusion model to individual slices, versus using a separate diffusion model trained on 3D patches. We will evaluate these methods on a dataset of brain MRI isotropic super-resolution images and assess the performance metrics of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
CONTROLS: Baselines will include the standard slice-by-slice application of the 2D model and a simple averaging strategy for combining the reconstructions from adjacent slices. The 3D diffusion model will be compared to these baselines under varying sizes of training datasets.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the 3D diffusion model to improve inter-slice consistency and reconstructed image quality, especially when trained on sufficiently large datasets. However, we anticipate difficulties in achieving high-quality 3D reconstructions, especially when dealing with smaller training datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncovering the Sources of Inter-Slice Inconsistency in 2D Slice-Wise Sampling
PROPOSAL: Analytically investigate how the intrinsic randomness of diffusion sampling contributes to inter-slice inconsistency in 3D medical reconstructions. We will derive a mathematical expression for the variance of the joint probability distribution of adjacent slices computed through the reverse diffusion process, assuming a standard 2D diffusion model and Poisson noise as measurement noise. This will help identify key parameters that control inter-slice inconsistency.
CONTROLS: We will compare our analysis to existing 1D diffusion processes and measure how the dimensionality affects the joint variance. Additionally, we will support our mathematical claims with numerical simulations using a simplified diffusion model and synthetic data.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our analysis will reveal that the dimensionality increase from 2D to 3D dominates the growth in joint variance, making it challenging to maintain consistent reconstructions across slices. Understanding this source of inconsistency will lay the groundwork for devising more effective remedies.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Designing a Cooperative 3D Denoising Scheme within Diffusion Sampling
PROPOSAL (Revised 2.): Building upon our analytical understanding of inter-slice inconsistency (Proposal 2), we will develop a novel 3D denoising scheme that allows adjacent slices to cooperate during the reverse diffusion process, aiming to reduce inter-slice discrepancies. We will inject stochastic noise into adjacent slices in a coordinated manner, based on the physics of diffusion, to enable a more direct exchange of information across slices.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed scheme to existing diffusion models and evaluate its performance on a range of 3D MRI data using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our cooperative denoising scheme is expected to significantly enhance inter-slice consistency and overall image quality in 3D medical reconstructions, making it a promising remedy for the challenges posed by diffusion-based 3D image reconstruction. However, we anticipate that the proposed scheme may still require fine-tuning for optimal performance on specific imaging tasks and anatomical structures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Impact of Temporal Synchronization on Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: Inspired by previous work in video restoration, we will investigate whether synchronizing stochastic noise components across adjacent slices can alleviate inter-slice inconsistency by mitigating the effects of uncoordinated diffusion sampling. We will apply a temporal synchronization scheme to the 2D diffusion model and evaluate its performance on a dataset of 3D MRI reconstructions, comparing it to the original unsynchronized diffusion model and our cooperative 3D denoising scheme (Revised Proposal 2).
CONTROLS: We will assess the impact of varying synchronization schemes, noise injection protocols, and diffusion model architectures on inter-slice consistency and reconstructed image quality.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Synchronizing stochastic noise components may have a positive effect on inter-slice consistency, but its efficacy might be limited by the complexity of 3D medical imaging and the inherent randomness of diffusion sampling, potentially leading to suboptimal performance compared to other remedies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-Augmentation Strategies for Enhancing 3D Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We will explore data-augmentation techniques, specifically rotations, translations, and mirror symmetries, to artificially increase variability in the 2D diffusion model and encourage more consistent reconstructions when applied to 3D medical data. We will evaluate the effectiveness of these strategies inReducing inter-slice inconsistency and improving overall image quality on a dataset of 3D MRI reconstructions.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to a baseline of standard data augmentation and to our previous proposals on temporal synchronization and cooperative 3D denoising.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Data augmentation is expected to have a beneficial effect on inter-slice consistency, as it would increase the robustness of the model to various transforms, and thus enhancing the model's ability to produce consistent reconstructions across slices. However, we anticipate that the gains might be limited, and other remedies, such as our cooperative 3D denoising scheme (Revised Proposal 2), might offer more substantial improvements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimizing the Trade-Off Between Inter-Slice Consistency and Fine Diagnostic Details
PROPOSAL: We will address the challenge of maintaining inter-slice consistency while preserving fine diagnostic details in 3D medical reconstructions. By leveraging the multi-resolution nature of diffusion models, we will develop an adaptive learning strategy that selectively amplifies or attenuates the spatial details in the reconstructed images, allowing for improved inter-slice consistency without compromising fine diagnostic detail recovery.
CONTROLS: We will compare our adaptive strategy to a baseline that uniformity applies diffusion model strength across spatial scales and evaluate them on a range of 3D MRI data, assessing inter-slice consistency and fine diagnostic detail recovery using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
COST: 110 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our adaptive learning strategy will offer an improved trade-off between inter-slice consistency and fine diagnostic detail recovery, potentially enabling higher-quality 3D medical reconstructions. However, we may need to select a parameter that controls the optimization process carefully to avoid either inconsistency or over-smoothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-Constrained Diffusion Models for Improved 3D Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: To address the limitations of current diffusion models in preserving inter-slice consistency, we will explore the use of physics-based regularization terms that incorporate prior knowledge about the underlying imaging physics. Specifically, we will modify the diffusion model to incorporate total variation (TV) regularization, which is widely used in image reconstruction tasks, to improve the spatial coherence and realism of the reconstructed images across slices.
CONTROLS: We will compare our physics-constrained diffusion model to the standard diffusion model and assess its performance on a dataset of 3D MRI reconstructions, evaluating inter-slice consistency and reconstructed image quality using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The addition of physics-based regularization terms is expected to improve inter-slice consistency and overall image quality, as well as help recover fine diagnostic details in 3D medical reconstructions. However, the effect of TV regularization might be limited, as it may over-smooth the images or remove fine details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning of 2D Models to 3D Reconstruction Tasks with Improved Inter-Slice Consistency
PROPOSAL: We will investigate whether pre-trained 2D diffusion models can be effectively adapted to 3D reconstruction tasks, leveraging the improvements in inter-slice consistency, without necessitating the training of new models from scratch. By fine-tuning the pre-trained 2D models on 3D data, we aim to achieve improved inter-slice consistency and adapted performance on specific 3D medical reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the transferred 2D models to standard 2D models trained from scratch and assess their performance on a dataset of 3D MRI reconstructions, evaluating inter-slice consistency, fine diagnostic details, and overall image quality using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Transfer learning is expected to offer an efficient way to adapt pre-trained 2D diffusion models to 3D reconstruction tasks, potentially achieving better inter-slice consistency and performance on specific 3D medical imaging tasks compared to training new 2D models from scratch. However, the performance gain might be limited, and more work may be required to fully leverage the benefits of transfer learning in this context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation of 3D Diffusion Models on Sparse-View and Limited-Angle CT Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will extend our investigation into 3D medical reconstruction with diffusion models to the challenging domain of sparse-view and limited-angle Computed Tomography (CT) reconstruction. We will evaluate the performance of our proposed 3D diffusion models, as well as various 2D models adapted to 3D using transfer learning, on a dataset of sparse-view CT scans, comparing their ability to reconstruct high-quality images under severely under-sampled conditions.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to standard CT reconstruction methods, such as filtered backprojection, and assess the performance of different models using metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist.
COST: 140 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our 3D diffusion models are expected to outperform 2D models in sparse-view and limited-angle CT reconstruction tasks, leveraging the advantages of 3D modeling to better capture anatomical structures and relationships under severe under-sampling conditions. However, the performance may be sensitive to the specific CT scanning protocol and data characteristics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Performance Comparison of 3D Diffusion Models for 3D Medical Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive performance comparison of the proposed 3D diffusion models, including novel schemes for improving inter-slice consistency, transfer learning of 2D models, and physics-constrained diffusion, on various 3D medical reconstruction tasks, such as sparse-view and limited-angle CT reconstruction, and brain MRI isotropic super-resolution. We will evaluate their performance using multiple image quality metrics, computational complexity, and visual evaluation by an expert radiologist, providing a systematic analysis and recommendations for the best practices for 3D diffusion-based 3D medical reconstruction.
CONTROLS: We will revisit and validate the performance of all previous proposals on a unified dataset to ensure a direct comparison.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comprehensive comparison will provide a thorough evaluation of the strengths and weaknesses of different 3D diffusion models, enabling researchers and clinicians to select the most suitable approach for various 3D medical reconstruction tasks and providing insights into potential future research directions.
